papers.title: Sex Differences in Stress Reactivity and Dementia Risk Across the Lifespan: A Social Safety Theory Perspective.
papers.abstract: Brain health is a key predictor of morbidity and mortality across the life course, and as the proportion of individuals experiencing cognitive decline grows larger, understanding sex differences in processes that drive cognitive aging in each sex is becoming increasingly important. To address this pressing need, we review research focusing on a central but frequently underappreciated factor: biopsychosocial stress reactivity. Examining this topic through the lens of Social Safety Theory, we first summarize known sex differences in psychological, neural, and biological stress reactivity, with a focus on how stress occurring across the lifespan can promote systemic chronic inflammation and lead to inflammation-related health problems, particularly for females. Next, we describe known sex differences in lifestyle behaviors and biological pathways that can both increase and decrease risk for stress-related health problems including dementia-namely, sleep, physical activity, diet, and sex steroid hormone dynamics. Finally, based on this research, we discuss several strategies for reducing stress-related dementia risk and improving cognitive resilience across the life course, highlighting the health monitoring approaches that will inform early intervention, and in turn, improved brain health for the older adults of tomorrow.

papers.title: Working memory supports cognitive control by orchestrating dimension-specific modulation during late conflict resolution.
papers.abstract: Working memory plays a central role in cognitive control, yet how it shapes target- and distractor-related processing over time remains unclear. Here, we combined a working memory load manipulation with a modified Stroop task in which distractors preceded targets. Behaviorally, we found that pre-exposure to the distractor eliminated the congruency effect, but this benefit was absent under high load. This pattern suggests that the benefit of advance distractor presentation is sensitive to concurrent working-memory demands. Electrophysiologically, the distractor-locked lateralized readiness potential (LRP) indicated that working-memory load altered distractor-related response activation before target onset. After target onset, load-related modulation emerged during late conflict resolution, as indexed by the sustained potential (SP), whereas earlier intervals associated with attentional selection (posterior N2) and conflict monitoring (N450) did not show load-dependent modulation. Time-frequency decoding and representational similarity analysis further revealed distinct spectro-temporal profiles of target- and distractor-related processing: target-related coding emerged earlier in the theta band (540-780 ms), consistent with stimulus-response mapping, whereas distractor-related coding emerged later in the mu-beta band (870-1180 ms), consistent with response-related regulation. These findings highlight dimension- and stage-specific patterns of working-memory modulation during conflict resolution.

papers.title: Metabolic Failure and EEG Abnormalities After Cardiac Arrest: Which Comes First, the Chicken or the Egg?
Integrative Multi-Omics Reveals Differential Mechanisms of Four TCM Formulations in Treating Insomnia via Syndrome-Compound-Metabolite Association Networks.
papers.abstract: Guipi Pills (GPW), Wuling Capsule (WLC), Bailemian Capsule (BLMC), and Zaoren Anshen Capsule (ZRASC) are representative traditional Chinese medicine formulations for treating insomnia based on different syndromes of Heart-Spleen Deficiency, Heart-Kidney Disharmony, Liver Qi Stagnation with Yin Deficiency, and Heart Blood Deficiency, respectively. However, their molecular mechanisms remain unclear. To elucidate the "same disease, different treatment" mechanisms of these four formulations against sleep deprivation-induced insomnia through an integrated multi-omics and network pharmacology strategy. Chemical constituents were characterized by UHPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS. A meta-analysis evaluated clinical differences and syndrome consistency. Subsequently, A mouse model of sleep deprivation was established; behavioral tests and HE/Nissl staining were performed. On this basis, fecal 16S rRNA gene sequencing, serum metabolomics, and hypothalamic transcriptomics were integrated to construct a microbiota-metabolite network. Furthermore, network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted component-target interactions. Finally, key protein expression was validated by western blot. UHPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS identified 87, 56, 163, and 128 compounds from GPW, WLC, BLMC, and ZRASC, respectively. Meta-analysis (62 RCTs, 6,045 patients) showed WLC and BLMC reduced PSQI scores alone or in combination; ZRASC benefited only in combination, and GPW combination benefit was borderline. Syndrome-efficacy interactions were inconsistent. In mice, all formulations alleviated neuronal damage despite heterogeneous behavioral improvements. All four formulations suppressed Alistipes and commonly reversed 39 serum metabolites enriched in glutathione metabolism and pentose phosphate pathway. Each formulation showed syndrome-related metabolic regulation. Hypothalamic transcriptomics revealed commonly downregulated genes (S100a9, Gbp5, Fpr1, Tnfsf8) and distinct patterns: lipid metabolism-immune suppression (GPW), transcriptional-metabolic inhibition (WLC), prolactin signaling (BLMC), and PPAR-driven energy repair (ZRASC). In an exploratory analysis, the number of microbiota-metabolite association pairs increased from WLC (158) to GPW (393), BLMC (836), and ZRASC (1,243); this gradient is hypothesis-generating and warrants independent validation.Network pharmacology and molecular docking predicted potential formulation-specific and common inflammatory pathway targets. Finally, western blot showed all formulations downregulated iNOS and COX2; all except WLC upregulated SLC7A11, GPX4, FTH, and Bcl2 (P < 0.05). In this study, these four formulations showed heterogeneous, syndrome-associated patterns across microbiota remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, anti-inflammation, and anti-ferroptosis, which may help generate hypotheses regarding the "same disease, different treatment" principle. The findings provide a mechanistic basis for clinical application and a methodological reference for TCM modernization.

papers.title: Preserved Choroidal Thickness and Vascularity Index in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Report No. 2 from the ORNET Study.
papers.abstract: In this prospective ORNET analysis, obstructive sleep apnea was not associated with significant changes in choroidal thickness or vascularity index as measured by optical coherence tomography, suggesting relative preservation of choroidal tissue.

papers.title: Phytocannabinoids in neurologic, neuropsychiatric, inflammatory, pain, cardiometabolic, hepatic, renal, and neoplastic disorders: Pharmacology, clinical evidence, and translational perspectives.
papers.abstract: Phytocannabinoids are pharmacologically diverse constituents of Cannabis sativa whose actions go beyond canonical cannabinoid receptors. Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) are best characterized, while cannabigerol, cannabidivarin, tetrahydrocannabivarin, cannabichromene, cannabinol, and related compounds are emerging candidates. This review integrates molecular pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, safety, and therapeutic evidence across neurologic, neuropsychiatric, inflammatory, pain, cardiovascular and metabolic, hepatic, renal, and neoplastic disorders. The strongest evidence supports pharmaceutical-grade oral CBD as adjunctive therapy for seizures associated with Dravet syndrome, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and tuberous sclerosis complex, and standardized THC-CBD formulations for selected patients with multiple sclerosis-associated spasticity. Emerging clinical signals in schizophrenia, pain, fibromyalgia, sleep disturbance, substance-use disorders, dermatologic conditions, sickle cell disease, and other symptom-focused indications support continued development. However, efficacy remains compound-, formulation-, exposure-, and indication-specific. In oncology, supportive-care applications must remain distinct from tumor-directed treatment, for which clinical efficacy has not been established. Preclinical studies show coherent effects on neuronal excitability, glial and immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrative stress, mitochondrial injury, fibrosis, and regulated cell death. These findings support further investigation in neurodegeneration, ischemia-reperfusion injury, diabetic cardiovascular disease, immune-mediated disorders, hepatic and renal injury, and selected cancers. Translation is constrained by product heterogeneity, variable exposure, uncertain target engagement, model differences, drug interactions, and underpowered trials. Standardized products, exposure-informed dosing, pharmacodynamic biomarkers, responder-enriched designs, and indication-specific randomized studies can address these barriers. Phytocannabinoids therefore represent a promising therapeutic platform whose potential will be best realized by matching defined compounds and formulations to biologically coherent diseases, mechanisms, treatment windows, and patient populations.

papers.title: Disrupted cortical signatures of response inhibition in Parkinson's disease revealed by TMS-EEG.
papers.abstract: Inhibitory control deficits are a hallmark of Parkinson's disease (PD), particularly in patients with L-DOPA-induced dyskinesias (LID), but the cortical mechanisms underlying impaired inhibition remain poorly understood. We used transcranial magnetic stimulation and electroencephalography (TMS-EEG) to investigate cortical dynamics during a Go/NoGo task in PD patients with and without LID, compared with healthy volunteers. Thirty-six PD patients (18 LID-PD, 18 nLID-PD) and 20 healthy volunteers performed a Go/NoGo task during TMS-EEG, which assessed functional connectivity between the supplementary motor area (SMA) and primary motor cortex (M1), and cortical reactivity through TMS-evoked potentials. Healthy volunteers exhibited task-dependent modulation of SMA-M1 connectivity, with increased theta-band coupling during NoGo trials and gamma-band coupling during Go trials; this pattern was absent in both PD groups, particularly in those with dyskinesias. TMS-evoked potentials revealed enhanced N100 responses during NoGo trials in healthy volunteers, reduced in non-dyskinetic patients and absent in dyskinetic ones. SMA-M1 gamma connectivity correlated with motor performance and clinical severity. During post-TMS epochs, healthy volunteers showed context-dependent alpha/beta modulation that was disrupted in PD patients. SMA-M1 communication and cortical inhibitory processing are impaired in PD, especially in patients with dyskinesias. SMA dysfunction may represent a biomarker and therapeutic target for inhibitory deficits in PD.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: Predicting cerebrospinal fluid α-synuclein seed amplification assay positivity in borderline hyposmia.
papers.abstract: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) α-synuclein seed amplification assays (SAAs) provide valuable biomarkers of underlying α-synuclein pathology. Although more severe olfactory impairment is associated with a higher likelihood of CSF α-syn SAA positivity in prodromal Parkinson's disease (PD), a simple tool to enrich candidates for CSF biomarker testing is lacking, particularly among individuals with borderline hyposmia. We aimed to develop and internally validate an exploratory clinical prediction model for CSF α-syn SAA positivity in this subgroup. A total of 83 participants with age- and sex-adjusted University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT) percentiles >15 and ≤ 20 were included from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) Phase 2 prodromal cohort. A prediction model was developed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression with 16 candidate predictors and 10-fold cross-validation. Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples repeating the complete model-development procedure. Among 83 participants, 43 (51.8%) were SAA-positive and 40 (48.2%) were SAA-negative. The LASSO model retained age, sex, REM Sleep Behavior Disorder Screening Questionnaire (RBDSQ) score, and Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) score. The apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.927, and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.896, with an optimism-corrected Brier score of 0.149. This exploratory four-variable LASSO model demonstrated promising discrimination for CSF α-syn SAA positivity among individuals with borderline hyposmia. External validation in larger, independent cohorts is required before clinical application.

papers.title: Long-term outcomes and cost-effectiveness of a modified electrocautery-assisted intracapsular tonsillectomy technique (E-ICT) for the pediatric population.
papers.abstract: Intracapsular tonsillectomy (ICT) may reduce postoperative morbidity compared with extracapsular tonsillectomy, but long-term outcomes of electrocautery-assisted ICT (E-ICT) remain incompletely characterized. This study evaluated long-term outcomes, safety, tonsillar regrowth, and parental satisfaction associated with E-ICT in children. This retrospective cohort study included 278 children aged 2-18 years who underwent E-ICT at a secondary care hospital in Saudi Arabia between 2015 and 2023. A one-time cross-sectional long-term assessment of the historical cohort was conducted during 2024-2026. Retrospective data included demographic, clinical, perioperative, and early postoperative outcomes. The one-time long-term assessment was obtained for 195 children (70.1%): the same structured parent-reported questionnaire was administered to all 195 children; 62 additionally underwent in-clinic physical examination including fiberoptic nasolaryngoscopy, whereas 133 completed the assessment by telephone/virtual contact. Outcomes included hemorrhage, healthcare utilization, symptom improvement, tonsillar regrowth, revision surgery, and long-term parent-reported satisfaction. Mean age was 6.48 years, and 78.4% underwent surgery for obstructive sleep-disordered breathing (oSDB). Primary hemorrhage occurred in 0.4% and secondary hemorrhage in 3.2%; 0.7% required operative intervention. Mean long-term follow-up was approximately 6 years. Recurrent tonsillitis improved in 98.5%, recurrent sore throat in 94.4%, and oSDB in 91.3%. Among 62 clinically examined children, tonsillar regrowth occurred in 9.7%, with one revision surgery; the overall revision rate was 0.4%. Long-term parent-reported satisfaction was high, with 94.9% rating the outcome as 4-5/5. E-ICT was associated with durable symptom improvement, low hemorrhage and revision rates, and high long-term parent-reported satisfaction, supporting its practicality in resource-limited healthcare settings.

papers.title: Patient perspectives on same-day discharge after elective minimally invasive colorectal surgery.
papers.abstract: Same-day discharge after minimally invasive colorectal surgery is increasingly implemented, yet little is known about patient perspectives. Incorporating these perspectives is essential to ensure that same-day discharge pathways remain patient-centered and aligned with recovery needs. A qualitative descriptive study was conducted among adults who underwent elective minimally invasive colectomy or stoma reversal planned for same-day discharge at a university-affiliated colorectal referral center (February 2020-March 2023). Semistructured telephone interviews with 12 core open-ended questions were performed postoperatively between June and August 2023. Purposeful sampling ensured variation in surgical indication, baseline characteristics, and same-day discharge success. Transcriptions were independently coded by 2 reviewers using an inductive thematic analysis. Of 191 patients planned for same-day discharge, 25 were approached and 17 completed interviews when thematic saturation was reached. Mean time from surgery to interview was 15.3 months (standard deviation 8.3). Mean age was 51 years (standard deviation 16), 58.8% were female, and colon cancer was the most common indication (n = 9). Four themes emerged: (1) need for preparedness and foresight, (2) adjusting to the homecare model, (3) comfort and return of daily function, and (4) factors limiting homecare. Patients emphasized preoperative education, social support, and timely access to care. Reported benefits included improved sleep, emotional comfort, and dietary freedom, whereas challenges involved wound care, injectable medications, and limited community resources. Despite initial hesitancy, most participants expressed satisfaction and willingness to choose same-day discharge again. Same-day discharge was perceived positively, given adequate preparation, home support, and timely access to services. Incorporating patient input may optimize same-day discharge protocols and recovery experiences.

papers.title: Identification and validation of circadian rhythm-related diagnostic biomarkers for endometriosis through integrating machine learning and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis (EMs) is a chronic inflammatory disease, and the lack of candidate molecular biomarkers remain a major clinical challenge. Circadian rhythm disruption plays a non-negligible role in EMs. However, the diagnostic potential of circadian rhythm-related biomarkers remains insufficiently validated. We performed weighted gene co-expression network analysis to screen for endometriosis-related hub modules. Four machine learning algorithms were used for feature selection in the training cohort, and the resulting diagnostic model was evaluated in three independent GEO validation cohorts. To evaluate the immune microenvironment, we applied MCPcounter, CIBERSORT, and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. Single‑cell RNA‑seq data were processed with Seurat for cell clustering and annotation, cell‑cell communication networks were constructed using CellChat, and pseudotime trajectory analysis was performed with Monocle. SMC2, SUV39H2, and TIMELESS were identified as candidate molecular biomarkers, demonstrating favorable diagnostic performance across three independent validation sets. Computational immune infiltration analysis suggested higher enrichment scores for B cells and CD8+ T cells, along with lower scores for Tregs and NK cells in EMs samples. Single-cell analysis revealed an increased proportion of mesenchymal cells in EMs samples and altered cell-cell communication involving BMP, CHEMERIN, and GRN signaling pathways. Pseudotime analysis further suggested transcriptional relationships among distinct stromal cell populations. This study identified SMC2, SUV39H2, and TIMELESS as candidate tissue-based molecular biomarkers for EMs and revealed alterations in stromal cell populations and immune-related features associated with the disease.
papers.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

papers.title: Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMIs) and Just-in-Time Adaptive Interventions (JITAIs) for sleep and circadian health: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Sleep and circadian disturbances are highly prevalent and contribute to impaired mood. Ecological momentary interventions (EMIs) and just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs) have emerged as promising approaches to address sleep and circadian disturbances by delivering real-time, context-aware support. However, their effectiveness for improving sleep, circadian, and mood outcomes has not been systematically appraised; therefore, this study aimed to characterize and evaluate these effects. A comprehensive search was conducted across six databases from inception to October 21, 2025, supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking of included studies. Two investigators independently screened studies, extracted data, and appraised methodological quality using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database (PEDro) scale. Standardized mean differences (SMD) were estimated for outcomes using random-effects models. Subgroup differences between EMIs and JITAIs were tested, and sensitivity analyses were conducted. Eleven RCTs (3 EMIs and 8 JITAIs) were identified from 4094 studies. Interventions varied in therapeutic framework, duration, and adaptive features. Pooled analyses demonstrated significant improvements in sleep efficiency (SMD = 0.71, 95% CI [0.17, 1.25]), reduction in insomnia severity (SMD = -0.87, 95% CI [-1.32, -0.42]), reduction in dysfunctional beliefs and attitudes about sleep (SMD = -0.96, 95% CI [-1.83, -0.09]), and reduction in depressive symptoms (SMD = -0.76, 95% CI [-1.23, -0.29]). The pooled effect on sleep quality did not reach statistical significance (SMD = -0.74, 95% CI [-1.49, 0.00]). Tests for subgroup differences between EMIs and JITAIs were not statistically significant for any outcome. None of the studies reported circadian outcomes. The findings suggest potential benefits for insomnia severity and depressive symptoms, but heterogeneity and the limited number of trials constrain conclusions about clinical importance. Inconsistent terminology, limited optimization, and heterogeneity in intervention designs demonstrate that this field remains in an early stage. Greater consistency in reporting, increased integration of objective monitoring, including measures of circadian processes, and incorporation of optimization processes may help realize the full potential of adaptive digital approaches.

papers.title: Specific learning disorders in children with epilepsy.
papers.abstract: It is estimated that between half and approximately 70% of children with epilepsy experience learning difficulties, making this a prominent issue during the school-age years. Possible causes include mild intellectual disability, comorbid neurodevelopmental disorders, and sleep disorders; among these, cases with comorbid specific learning disorder (SLD) are by no means rare. In particular, regarding developmental dyslexia, which is the most common condition, it has been reported to be frequent in conditions associated with the left temporal lobe, such as self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE), and periventricular heterotopia (PNH). Reports of developmental dysgraphia have also been noted in TLE and SeLECTS. Overall, it has been reported that children with epilepsy tend to have lower math skills. It is known that the severity is higher in idiopathic generalized epilepsy than in focal epilepsy, and it is speculated that this involves networks such as the parietal lobe and impairments in working memory. Since epilepsy can cause SLD symptoms due to various anatomical abnormalities and the development of electrical networks, it is important to consider SLD as one of the causes of learning difficulties when providing clinical care for epilepsy.

papers.title: Real-world efficacy and safety profile of sulthiame treatment in drug-resistant childhood epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Sulthiame (STM) is a potent carbonic anhydrase inhibitor primarily used in focal epilepsy syndromes; however, clinical data regarding its efficacy and safety in broader drug-resistant childhood epilepsy remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy, electroencephalographic response, and safety profile of STM in a cohort of pediatric patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. A retrospective medical chart review was conducted for patients under 18 years of age treated with STM at a tertiary pediatric neurology clinic between 2011 and 2024. Data including demographic characteristics, etiology, seizure semiology, epilepsy syndromes, treatment duration, and dosage were analyzed. Electroencephalographic (EEG) findings were assessed using EEG recordings obtained within 1-3 months after initiation of sulthiame therapy. Seizure frequency outcomes were assessed by comparing baseline seizure frequency with seizure frequency at the final available clinical follow-up. Sixty-one patients (55.7% female; median seizure onset: 14 months) were included. A structural etiology was identified in 50.8% of patients, and 62.3% had a well-defined epilepsy syndrome. At the final available clinical follow-up, 41% (n = 25) of patients achieved complete seizure freedom, while 16.4% (n = 10) showed a ≥ 50% reduction in seizure frequency. Conversely, 42.6% demonstrated a < 50% reduction. A higher number of previously failed anti-seizure medications (ASMs) was significantly associated with a poorer treatment response (p = 0.014). EEG improvement was observed in 44.3% of the cohort. Notably, focal seizure semiology was associated with favorable EEG outcomes, whereas combined semiology was linked to electroencephalographic worsening (p = 0.026). STM was generally well-tolerated; adverse effects were reported in only nine patients, with treatment discontinuation required in only two cases (3.2%). Sulthiame is an effective and well-tolerated therapeutic option for children with drug-resistant epilepsy, particularly those with focal semiology. Our findings suggest that a higher burden of prior ASM treatment negatively impacts response rates, highlighting the potential benefit of considering STM earlier in the treatment algorithm for specific pediatric populations.

papers.title: MRgFUS for drug-resistant epilepsy: Preliminary report for prospective clinical trial.
papers.abstract: To assess the safety, feasibility, and preliminary clinical outcomes of magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). This TFDA-regulated, open-label study enrolled four adults with DRE. MRgFUS targeted the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT), the centromedian nucleus (CM), the posterior corpus callosum (CC), or the hypothalamic hamartoma (HH). The primary endpoints were safety and feasibility, while secondary endpoints included seizure frequency, EEG results, and postoperative MRI findings. The mean age of the patients was 34.7 years and the mean SDR was 0.38. Two of the procedures were performed under local anesthesia and three under general anesthesia. No serious adverse events, permanent neurological deficit, or postoperative cognitive decline were observed. At follow-up ranging from 3 to 15 months, seizure outcomes varied. The CM-treated patient showed stable overall seizure frequency with a 42.6% reduction in focal seizures. Posterior CC lesioning reduced interhemispheric EEG synchrony and was associated with a 15.9% reduction in generalized seizures. The HH case displayed a decrease in epileptiform activity on EEG and a 55.5% reduction of gelastic seizures, despite the absence of a definitive lesion. In the ANT case, the initial procedure was discontinued prior to reaching therapeutic temperatures, and the repeat treatment under general anesthesia was associated with a 66.0% seizure reduction at final follow-up. MRgFUS achieved lesion formation at selected epilepsy-related targets, including the first reported applications to the posterior CC and CM for epilepsy. However, the ability to achieve therapeutic temperatures and produce a definitive lesion varied among patients and was influenced by skull characteristics of the anatomical target. Given the small, heterogeneous cohort and limited follow-up, the observed clinical outcomes should be considered preliminary. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to establish efficacy and optimize treatment parameters.

papers.title: Large Vision-Language Models for Pediatric Motor Tic Detection: Case-Control Diagnostic Study.
papers.abstract: Clinical diagnosis of tic disorders (TDs) is often delayed by fluctuating symptoms and the subjective nature of assessments. While automated methods have been proposed to bridge this gap, traditional machine learning models frequently lack robustness in unconstrained environments and fail to capture the complex, multisite tics characteristic of severe TDs. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a fine-tuned large vision-language model framework for the automated, interpretable detection of pediatric motor tics, addressing the clinical need for objective and efficient symptom assessment in unconstrained environments. In this multicenter study, 168 pediatric participants (n=83, 49.4% with TDs and n=85, 50.6% healthy controls) underwent 12-hour continuous video-electroencephalography monitoring. We fine-tuned the Qwen3-VL-8B model using 3- to 5-minute video segments via low-rank adaptation. The framework used chain-of-thought prompting to generate both binary classifications and textual justifications. A strict patient-wise split ensured zero identity overlap between training and test sets. Diagnostic precision was evaluated using 95% CIs calculated with the Clopper-Pearson exact method. In total, 168 pediatric participants (age: mean 8.3, SD 2.3 years) were enrolled, providing 559 expert-validated video segments for analysis. On the independent test set (n=55), the framework achieved 89.1% (49/55; 95% CI 77.8%-95.9%) accuracy and an area under the curve of 0.950 (95% CI 0.892-1.000), significantly outperforming the landmark-based deep neural network (accuracy 74.1%; P=.004); recall reached 100% (25/25 positive episodes; 95% CI 86.3%-100.0%). Model-generated justifications showed substantial agreement with expert annotations (κ=0.784, 95% CI 0.625-0.943; P<.001). These findings suggest that a vision-language model framework can capture clinically relevant tic features beyond conventional geometric descriptors. By combining high sensitivity (recall) with text-based diagnostic justifications aligned with clinical severity dimensions (eg, frequency and intensity), the approach may support automated video review and preliminary symptom quantification in controlled monitoring settings.

papers.title: Young-Onset Parkinson's Disease with Heterozygous VPS13C Variants: A Case Series and Review of Pathogenic Implications.
papers.abstract: Young-onset Parkinson's disease (YOPD) is characterized by the onset of parkinsonism before 50 years of age and has a strong genetic contribution. Homozygous mutations in the VPS13C gene have been implicated in autosomal recessive YOPD; however, the clinical significance of heterozygous variants remains unclear. We describe four patients with YOPD who were found to carry heterozygous VPS13C. In these patients, onset ranged from 37 to 45 years of age. All patients had asymmetric onset of motor symptoms and demonstrated good response to levodopa therapy. Three patients had tremor as the initial symptom. Non-motor features included rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder in all patients, hyposmia in two patients, hallucinations in two patients, and neuropsychiatric symptoms. Two patients carried additional heterozygous glucosylceramidase beta (GBA) mutations. Brain magnetic resonance imaging was normal in all patients. Genetic testing revealed heterozygous VPS13C variants in all cases. This case series describes the clinical characteristics of four patients with YOPD carrying heterozygous VPS13C variants of uncertain significance. Although these observations expand the phenotypic spectrum of patients harboring VPS13C variants, the pathogenic contribution of these variants remains uncertain and requires further genetic and functional validation.
papers.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology

papers.title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol.
papers.abstract: Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support. We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)-executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention's effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion. The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027. This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-based machine learning models for hyperacute detection of large vessel occlusion stroke.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has shown potential as a prehospital triage instrument for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO-a) stroke. In this study, we determined the diagnostic accuracy of EEG-based machine learning algorithms for LVO-a stroke detection. Anterior circulation large vessel occlusion stroke detection machine learning models were developed using EEG data from the ELECTRA-STROKE (NCT03699397) and AI-STROKE (NCT05437237) studies. Single 2- to 3-min EEG recordings were obtained using 8 dry electrodes in adults with suspected stroke in prehospital and in-hospital settings. Patients with a clean EEG segment of ≥ 5 s (visually selected) were included and EEG symmetry features were extracted. We assessed the performance of multiple machine learning models using nested cross-validation (CV), optimising models with 3-fold CV (inner loop) and evaluating them with leave-one-out CV (outer loop). Of 1293 patients with suspected stroke, 336 (26%) were included (74% prehospital, 26% in-hospital). Median age was 72 (IQR 61-80) years, and 231 (69%) were male. Sixteen (5%) patients had LVO-a stroke, 140 (42%) non-LVO-a ischaemic stroke, 52 (15%) TIA, 13 (4%) haemorrhagic stroke and 115 (34%) a stroke mimic. Naïve Bayes achieved the highest observed area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.85 [95% CI, 0.77-0.93]), with a sensitivity of 69% (95% CI, 44%-86%) and specificity of 86% (95% CI, 82%-89%). Machine learning models for LVO-a stroke detection based solely on EEG showed moderately high diagnostic accuracy. These results support the potential of EEG-based LVO-a stroke detection, but improved EEG data acquisition is needed before clinical implementation can be considered.

papers.title: Neuromodulatory effects of audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training on subjective tinnitus, a HD-EEG study protocol.
papers.abstract: Tinnitus affects 14% of the global population, with 2% experiencing a severe form of the condition. Sound therapy using white noise emitted by hearing aids is a common intervention, supported by the phenomenon of residual inhibition observed during tinnitus assessment. This study aims to investigate whether audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training can improve the quality of life of patients with chronic subjective tinnitus by enabling them to listen to their own phonation, which may mask the tinnitus or induce residual inhibition. We will conduct a prospective, controlled, monocentric, 2-arm block-randomized study, stratified by the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI) score, involving two groups for two sequential phases (Phase 1 and Phase 2). Fifty-six patients with tinnitus, recruited from the Ear Nose Throat (ENT) Department of Orléans University Hospital, will undergo a five-week training program, randomized into weekly remote group workshops, and daily individual sessions using specially developed videos. Training efficacy will be assessed through self-report questionnaires. The primary endpoint, the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, will be assessed at three ENT medical visits: at inclusion, end of phase 1 and end of phase 2. Additionally, patients in both groups will regularly complete Visual Analog Scales for Tinnitus and five related questions (noise, cervical, jaw, sleep, stress-anxiety) via a secure digital platform throughout the study. High-density electroencephalograms (HD-EEG) will be performed in a blinded manner before and after Phase 1 at the Neurology Department of Orléans University Hospital. This pilot study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of audio-proprio-phonatory training in patients with chronic subjective tinnitus and to objectively measure its effects using HD-EEG. We will explore potential correlations between changes brain activity (such as functional brain connectivity) and clinical responses to the intervention.

papers.title: Alcohol use disorder with metabolic dysfunction is associated with adverse sleep outcomes in a US clinical cohort.
papers.abstract: Sleep is critical to health, yet its relationship to metabolic dysfunction (MD) in alcohol use disorder (AUD) remains understudied in US clinical populations. 1359 participants were recruited through the Natural History Protocol at the National Institutes of Health and categorized into four groups: healthy controls (HC), individuals with MD only (metHC), individuals with current AUD without MD (AUD), and individuals with both current AUD and MD (metAUD). Sleep was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Multinomial logistic regression models were used to test associations between sleep metrics and group status, adjusting for age, race, and sex (Model 1), and additionally for education, income, and smoking status (Model 2). Additional models examined sleep outcomes by MD severity (mild, <3; severe, ≥3 criteria) among AUD. Thousand two hundred twenty participants were included: 155 HC, 397 metHC, 77 AUD, and 591 metAUD. Adverse sleep outcomes were associated with increased odds of metHC, AUD, and metAUD groups compared to HC, with the strongest associations observed for metAUD across multiple PSQI domains. Each one-category increase in sleep disturbance was associated with an eleven-fold increase in odds of metAUD relative to HC (OR: 11.71, 95% CI, 6.90-19.86). Associations remained significant in Model 2. Sleep disturbance and daytime dysfunction were also associated with increased odds of severe MD compared to AUD-only (false discovery rate < 0.05). Adverse sleep outcomes were associated with increased odds of co-occurring MD in AUD, highlighting the clinical relevance of monitoring both sleep and metabolic health and the need for targeted intervention in this population.

papers.title: A Kampo medicine, kamishoyosan, ameliorates menstruation-associated symptoms in patients with premenstrual syndrome: An exploratory open-label, randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a psychological or physical symptom. We conducted an open-label, randomized, exploratory trial with the aim of evaluating the efficacy and safety of kamishoyosan (KSS) for PMS. KSS was administered orally during three menstrual cycles. The primary endpoint was the change in the premenstrual Menstrual Distress Questionnaire (MDQ) total score. The secondary endpoints included MDQ total and subscale scores, a daily symptom questionnaire, the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment (WPAI) Questionnaire, overall impressions, sleep status, and heart rate. A total of 50 patients were enrolled. The primary endpoint, the premenstrual MDQ total score, was significantly ameliorated after KSS treatment. Furthermore, KSS reduced MDQ scores during the menstrual cycle. Among the MDQ subscales, KSS decreased score of pain, concentration, behavioral change, and negative feelings during the premenstrual cycle. In addition, hyperthymia reduced during the menstrual cycle. The results of the daily symptom questionnaire indicated that KSS treatment alleviated irritability, easy anger, anxiety, emotional instability, abdominal distension, coldness, and stiff shoulders.The WPAI activity impairment score was lower in the KSS group, and overall impression favoured in KSS treatment.. The only adverse event related to KSS was headache in one case. These exploratory findings suggest that KSS may improve menstrual-related symptoms in PMS.

papers.title: The Horizontal Split Technique for Posterior Pharyngeal Flap Surgery: Speech and Airway Outcomes in 220 Patients.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveThe purpose of this 10-year retrospective review was to report our single-center outcomes using the posterior pharyngeal flap (PPF) horizontal split technique to treat patients with syndromic and non-syndromic velopharyngeal dysfunction (VPD).DesignRetrospective review (2011-2021).SettingA tertiary pediatric institution.PatientsPatients with VPD (4-21 years old).InterventionsPPF surgery using the horizontal split inset technique by 2 surgeons.Main Outcome MeasuresEvaluated factors included demographics, VPD characteristics, and pre-operative speech evaluation. Evaluated outcomes included complications, revisional VPD surgery rates, post-operative resonance, nasometry scores, and the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI).ResultsTwo hundred and twenty children (median age: 6.9 years) underwent surgery. The median operative time was 47 min. Most patients (95%) achieved improved resonance, with 89% achieving mild or no hypernasality. Median nasalance scores significantly decreased (pre-operative: 42, post-operative: 18). Of 137 patients who underwent a post-operative polysomnogram, 18 patients had an AHI ≥5; 2 patients with syndromic diagnoses underwent PPF takedown. Ten patients underwent revisional VPD surgery. Patients with 22qDS (22q11.2 deletion syndrome) or non-cleft VPD had an increased risk of demonstrating significant residual hypernasality requiring revisional surgery.ConclusionsThis simple, reproducible PPF surgical technique yields reliably improved resonance in patients with syndromic and non-syndromic VPD. Patients with 22qDS and those with non-cleft VPD may have higher odds of demonstrating residual hypernasality and needing additional surgery. Although there is low risk of flap takedown for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), long-term airway monitoring remains essential.

papers.title: Squalamine prevents motor and non-motor symptoms in the paraquat and lectin rat model of the body-first subtype of Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Increasing evidence supports the existence of a distinct body-first subtype of Parkinson's disease (PD), in which the initial site of pathology is in the gut. Animal models that recapitulate the body-first subtype of PD are needed. We tested the hypothesis that non-motor features of the body-first subtype of PD are recapitulated in the paraquat and lectin (P + L) rat model of PD, a model that has previously demonstrated the pathological motor progression of this subtype of PD. Then, we tested whether oral squalamine, a gastrointestinal prokinetic that has been shown to reduce formation of pathological α-synuclein, could prevent pathology, motor, and non-motor findings. Rats (n = 93) were orally gavaged for seven days with paraquat (1 mg/kg) and lectin (0.05%) in 1% sucrose solution. A subset of rats (n = 37) were given 30 days of squalamine (20 mg/kg) in their drinking water immediately following P + L treatment. Rats were tested for parkinsonian motor deficits, gastrointestinal dysmotility, sleep abnormalities, and cognitive deficits. Rats were euthanized and their brains processed for phospho-S129-α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration. We show that the P + L rat model recapitulates non-motor features and pathology of gastrointestinal dysmotility and sleep abnormalities seen in the body-first subtype of PD. We show that oral squalamine prevents motor deficits, gastrointestinal dysmotility, and sleep abnormalities, and diminishes phospho-S129-α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration in the nigrostriatal pathway. We show that the P + L rat model recapitulates many features of the body-first subtype of PD and provides pre-clinical evidence for the use of squalamine to mitigate progression in the body-first subtype of PD.

papers.title: Chronotherapy leveraging dietary context overcomes circadian rhythm influence on cancer cell response to PPAR antagonists.
papers.abstract: Circadian physiology coordinates systemic and cellular metabolism through a light-entrained central clock and metabolically synchronized peripheral clocks. Whether feeding-fasting cycles or tumor-intrinsic clocks primarily set tumor metabolic state is unclear. Here, we profiled colorectal cancer (CRC) responses to PPAR antagonists across 2D and 3D CRC models and tumor-bearing mice. In standard high-glucose, low-fat medium, Bmal1 oscillations and daily variation in PPAR antagonist sensitivity were apparent in CRC cells. By contrast, nutrient-defined media that recapitulate feeding and nighttime fasting abolished time-dependent variability and unified drug responses across models. Still, the fed state selectively sensitized spheroids and patient-derived organoids to PPAR-γ antagonism. In mice, dosing PPAR-γ antagonist in the fed state prolonged survival and reduced hepatotoxicity. The use of Bmal-1-silenced CRC cells validated that feeding-fasting rhythms, not tumor-intrinsic clocks, govern CRC sensitivity to PPAR antagonists. Our study also supports the predictive capacity of nutrient-alternating 3D tumor models, enabling metabolism-targeted anticancer treatment evaluation.

papers.title: Internal chaos - the metabolic consequences of circadian dyssynchrony.
Semilunar nucleus neurons are highly excitable and potentiated by group I mGluRs to drive descending excitation to the mouse MNTB.
papers.abstract: Medial nucleus of the trapezoid body (MNTB) neurons receive one of the largest synapses in the mammalian brain, the calyx of Held; however, multiple studies reported additional non-calyceal excitatory inputs of largely unresolved origin to MNTB neurons. Most recently, the semilunar nucleus (SLN) was identified as a potential source of such non-calyceal input in the rat. To elucidate the function of this novel pathway, we investigated the connectivity and physiology of the mouse SLN, with particular focus on neuromodulation by group I metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs). Viral tracing not only confirmed the SLN-MNTB pathway in mice, but also revealed that MNTB-projecting SLN neurons received their input from the ipsilateral auditory cortex. Physiological characterization of SLN neurons using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings showed that SLN neurons, unlike most other auditory brainstem neurons, were intrinsically highly excitable. Electrical stimulation of the fibre tracts located dorsal to the SLN, evoked small, slow AMPA receptor-mediated EPSCs in SLN neurons that readily summated temporally. Immunolabeling revealed a heterogeneous expression of mGluR1 and mGluR5 across SLN neurons. A subpopulation of SLN neurons exhibited spontaneous action potential firing at resting membrane potential. Pharmacological activation of group I mGluRs further increased spontaneous firing of SLN neurons. Probing for functional connectivity between SLN and the ipsilateral MNTB, fibre tracts dorsal and lateral to the MNTB were stimulated, eliciting primarily non-calyceal AMPA receptor-mediated EPSCs in MNTB neurons. These findings suggest that SLN output may provide a glutamatergic tonic drive to MNTB neurons, potentially modulating their temporal processing. KEY POINTS: MNTB receives a descending input from the ipsilateral auditory cortex via SLN. SLN neurons are highly excitable during development and into maturation, with a subset exhibiting spontaneous firing at resting membrane potential. Descending glutamatergic input to SLN is small and slow, and shows consistent temporal summation. Group I mGluRs further enhance spontaneous firing of SLN neurons and both mGluR1 and mGluR5 are expressed in the SLN. Descending ipsilateral projections to MNTB neurons primarily drive glutamatergic, non-calyceal inputs.

papers.title: Respiratory phase orchestrates human olfactory cortical dynamics.
papers.abstract: Olfaction is fundamental to perception, memory, and emotion, yet the neural basis of human odor processing remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that odor-evoked brain activity is organized by respiratory phase-not absolute time-revealing that natural breathing structures olfactory cortical dynamics. Using simultaneous nasal respiration and electroencephalography recordings in [Formula: see text] participants, we delivered naturalistic odors (peppermint, oregano, and grapefruit) synchronized to individual breathing cycles. Odor presentation elicited respiratory phase-locked event-related spectral perturbations (RPL-ERSPs) in frontal and temporal regions, emerging during the first breath after stimulus onset. The most discriminative neural signatures were theta-band activity during inhalation and alpha-band activity during exhalation, patterns that were obscured in traditional time-locked analyses due to natural variability in breath duration. Leave-one-subject-out cross-validation of RPL-ERSPs achieved reliable odor detection (peppermint: AUC [Formula: see text] 0.79; oregano: AUC [Formula: see text] 0.67; grapefruit: AUC [Formula: see text] 0.62), establishing that phase-locked features generalize across individuals. To connect neural responses to perceptual experience without relying on odor naming-which can be disproportionately impaired in some populations-we quantified odor recognition using free-response descriptions scored with a semantic-similarity approach. Behavioral recognition strength paralleled the neural decoding hierarchy across odors, establishing the perceptual validity of RPL-ERSPs. RPL-ERSPs revealed rapid habituation, with decoding performance declining over repeated presentations, due to selective degradation of the most informative phase-locked features. These findings establish respiratory rhythm as a temporal scaffold for human olfactory cortical processing, positioning RPL-ERSPs as a sensitive, task-free approach for assessing olfactory function. We provide an open-source, respiration-synchronized olfactometer design to enable replication and adoption.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: Self-Reported Disease Severity and Treatment Experience among Individuals Reporting Healthcare Professional-Diagnosed Chronic Hand Eczema: Findings from the Cross-Sectional CHECK-US Study.
papers.abstract: Chronic hand eczema (CHE) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease with persistent symptoms that exert substantial clinical burden on patients. Real‑world data on CHE patient experience remain limited in the USA. This study aimed to assess symptoms across different severity and treatment groups and describe treatments, signs, and symptoms in participants with self‑reported CHE in the USA. This online cross-sectional survey included adults (aged 18-69 years) with self-reported CHE, recruited through general population panels. Subgroups were based on (1) participants' worst self-evaluated CHE severity in the past 12 months using a photographic guide as mild, moderate, and severe, and within those with moderate to severe CHE, as a subset with suboptimal response to topical corticosteroids (TCS); and (2) current treatments (systemics/phototherapy, TCS, topicals, no treatment, and never treated). Participants reported TCS use/experience and flare experience. Symptom severity (itch, pain, sleep disturbance) over past 24 h was assessed using visual analog scales (VAS). Among 982 participants with healthcare-professional (HCP)-diagnosed CHE, 87.8% reported their CHE as moderate to severe in the past 12 months. Most participants (79.7%) reported being treated currently for CHE, with 31.8% on TCS. At the time of survey, 62.9% reported a flare, with increased itch being the most common symptom. Participants with moderate to severe (versus mild) signs experienced increased itch, redness, and appearance of new skin lesions (p < 0.05). Spreading of lesions was more common among participants with suboptimal response to TCS (p = 0.006). Overall, itch had the highest mean (SD) VAS score of 5.0 (2.8). Symptom severity was notably higher among those receiving systemic treatments/phototherapy versus TCS. Moderate to severe CHE was common among participants, with TCS alone (without concurrent systemic or phototherapy use) being the most frequently observed treatment option. Participants with CHE continue to experience signs/symptoms despite receiving treatment, underscoring the need for more effective treatment options. Graphical abstract available for this article.

papers.title: Forward-backward translation and content validity study of the German version of the Patient-Reported Apnea Questionnaire.
papers.abstract: Health-related quality of life (HRQOL) assessment is an important component of chronic disease management, providing insights beyond clinical parameters. In obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), no comprehensive German-language patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) is currently available for routine clinical use. This study aims to adapt the Patient-Reported Apnea Questionnaire (PRAQ), a validated OSA-specific HRQOL instrument, for German-speaking patients. The German adaptation of the PRAQ followed a forward-backward translation process involving three translators. After harmonization, content validity was assessed through cognitive interviews with 20 OSA patients and an online survey among 14 sleep medicine experts. Feedback from both groups was incorporated into the final version of the questionnaire. The translation and adaptation process was conducted between April 2025 and March 2026. Two forward translations, one back-translation, and a final harmonization were performed. Patients identified issues mainly related to item relevance, conceptual overlap and response formats in the domains of daily activity, emotions and social interactions. Experts confirmed overall good comprehensibility but highlighted some concerns regarding item relevance and response scales. Based on patient and expert feedback, eight modifications were implemented, including clarifications of OSA-related terms, response options, and specific item wording, resulting in the final German PRAQ version. The German version of the PRAQ demonstrates decent content validity and comprehensibility, while reflecting the heterogeneous experiences of patients with OSA. Although some items were considered less relevant by certain patients, no essential domains were identified as missing. The study was approved by the ethics committee of the ​ University of Duisburg-Essen (25-12560-BO), and all participants provided written informed consent.

papers.title: Volume status as a potential state-dependent modifier of obstructive sleep apnea severity in chronic kidney disease and dialysis: a narrative review.
papers.abstract: This narrative review examines whether volume status may act as an underrecognized, state-dependent modifier of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and dialysis-dependent kidney failure. The main question was which links between extracellular volume, rostral fluid shift, and OSA are supported by empirical studies, and which implications for assessment and treatment remain hypothesis-generating. Evidence was synthesized from thematic searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to May 1, 2026, supplemented by reference-list review. An integrative narrative approach used purposive study selection and qualitative interpretation rather than systematic screening, pooled analysis, or formal risk-of-bias assessment. Sleep apnea is common in CKD and end-stage kidney disease, particularly when objective testing is used. Small physiological and imaging studies, mainly in hemodialysis patients, associate fluid overload and regional fluid measures with sleep apnea severity. Responses to fluid removal are heterogeneous, and some intervention studies include both obstructive and central events. These findings do not establish a reproducible volume-sensitive OSA phenotype. Effects on sleep-study timing, positive airway pressure (PAP) requirements, residual events, drug-induced sleep endoscopy, and upper-airway intervention outcomes remain unestablished. Volume status is a plausible state-dependent modifier of OSA severity in selected patients, supported predominantly by small dialysis studies. Distinguishing systemic from regional fluid and transient measurement states from reproducible patient characteristics provides a framework for testable hypotheses. Current evidence does not justify changes to sleep-study scheduling, PAP management, or upper-airway treatment selection.
