papers.title: Reduced diagnostic accuracy of screening questionnaires in older psychiatric patients at risk for obstructive sleep apnea: an observational cohort study.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is highly prevalent among geriatric patients and is associated with increased mortality, reduced quality of life, depression, and cognitive decline. Early identification and treatment are particularly important in older psychiatric patients, in whom typical OSA symptoms overlap with psychiatric and aging-related symptoms. Screening questionnaires are used to identify patients at risk for OSA, but their performance in older psychiatric populations is largely unknown. This study compared the diagnostic accuracy of screening questionnaires between younger and older psychiatric inpatients at risk for OSA and assessed the discriminative value of chronological age alone. Observational study of consecutive admissions to a psychiatric ward at University Hospital Erlangen (June 2016-December 2022). 128 screened patients at risk for OSA with valid overnight polygraphy and questionnaire data were analyzed (72 aged 18-64 years; 56 aged ≥ 65 years). Risk scores were calculated for STOP-Bang, STOP-B28, BOAH, GOAL, NoSAS and No-Apnea questionnaires. The reference standard was apnea-hypopnea-index (AHI) measured by polygraphy. Primary outcome measures were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity and specificity for any OSA (AHI ≥ 5 events/h). The discriminative value of age and individual questionnaire components was evaluated in the entire cohort. In the screened cohort of psychiatric inpatients, older patients had higher median AHI (7.7 vs. 1.8 events/h; p = 0.007), greater prevalence of any OSA (AHI ≥ 5: 73.2% vs. 47.2%; p = 0.003), deeper desaturations and longer apneas. In younger patients, questionnaire AUCs ranged 0.61-0.78. In the older subgroup, AUCs were 0.12-0.36 lower; BOAH had the highest AUC (0.59), while the other questionnaires showed AUCs of 0.38-0.49. The lower discrimination was mainly reflected in lower specificity. Chronological age yielded an AUC of 0.70 (95% CI, 0.61-0.80), whereas BMI, neck circumference, and symptom-based items showed poor discrimination. In our sample of psychiatric inpatients at risk for OSA, commonly used screening questionnaires demonstrated markedly reduced diagnostic performance in patients aged ≥ 65 years, largely reflecting lower specificity. Chronological age demonstrated moderate discriminative value. Further research is warranted regarding the accuracy of OSA screening in older patients, and a lower threshold for device-based diagnostics may warrant consideration.

papers.title: Inflammatory biomarkers of obstructive sleep apnea: a comprehensive review from known to novel.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a frequent condition that disrupts breathing during sleep and contributes to cardiovascular, metabolic, and cognitive problems. While intermittent hypoxia and oxidative stress are well known mechanisms, inflammation has gained attention as a central driver of disease. In recent years, researchers have examined a wide range of inflammatory biomarkers, from established ones such as tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), c-reactive protein (CRP), and interleukins, to newer candidates including interferon gamma (IFN-γ), fractalkine, serum amyloid A (SAA), monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), toll-like receptor (TLR), YKL-40, S100 proteins, neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet to lymphocyte ratio (PLR), galectin-3, neopterin, and pentraxin 3 (PTX3). Many of these markers show links with OSA severity and cardiovascular risk, though findings are not always consistent. Treatment with continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) can lower some inflammatory markers, suggesting a role for biomarker monitoring in therapy. At the same time, advances in omics and artificial intelligence are opening new paths for discovery of novel biomarkers. This review aims to bring together current knowledge on classical and new inflammatory biomarkers in OSA, and to outline their potential roles in screening diagnosis, risk assessment, and treatment for the future studies.

papers.title: Developing a Chinese value set for the FACT-8D, a cancer-specific multi-attribute utility instrument based on the FACT-general (FACT-G) questionnaire.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop a Chinese value set for the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-8 Dimensions (FACT-8D), a cancer-specific preference-based utility instrument derived from the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-General (FACT-G), to support the generation of QALY-based evidence for cost-utility analyses in oncology decision-making in China. An online discrete choice experiment (DCE) was conducted among a nationally representative sample of the Chinese general population, recruited through quota sampling based on age, gender and residence. Each respondent completed 16 choice sets, with each set comprising two hypothetical health states defined by the eight FACT-8D dimensions, along with an associated survival duration. Conditional logistic regression was used to model preferences, parameterized within the quality-adjusted life year (QALY) framework. Post-stratification weights were applied to adjust for sampling non-representativeness. Utility decrements were derived from the estimated trade-offs between health problems and survival time. The analysis included data from 2785 respondents who successfully completed the online survey. The largest utility decrements were associated with severe problems related to Pain, Nausea, and Sleep. In contrast, dimensions such as Social support, Work problems, and Worry were associated with comparatively smaller decrements. The worst possible health state was valued at - 0.153, indicating a state considered worse than being dead. This study developed the first Chinese value set for the FACT-8D, reflecting societal preferences for cancer-related health outcomes. The value set enables the use of FACT-8D in cost-utility analyses of oncology interventions in China.
papers.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

papers.title: How Does Sleep Deprivation Rewrite the Cognitive Function in the Hippocampus?
papers.abstract: In the modern society, sleep loss has become a global concern. Sleep deprivation (SD), a special type of complete acute or chronic sleep loss, swiftly erodes cognitive functions with observed structural and functional changes in the brain according to previous research. Hippocampus, especially its cornu ammonis 1 region presenting density in cognition-critical pyramidal neurons and complex inter-cellular crosstalk, is particularly vulnerable to sleep loss. SD disrupts hippocampal structure and function, leading to cognitive deficits. Mechanistically, by uncoupling energy-redox homeostasis, SD silences plasticity-promoting signals and neuron-glia interactions while amplifying neuroinflammation and metabolic deficits, thereby disrupting synaptic efficacy, network synchrony, waste removal procedure, and neurogenesis across the hippocampus and its related circuits. Although several pharmacological and non-pharmacological translational attempts have been announced, more efforts are in demand for advanced multi-modal models and cohorts integrating transcriptomics, connectomics, and real-time neuromodulation for elucidating the cascading mechanisms of SD-induced cognitive deficits in the hippocampus, as well as for interventions restoring sleep-dependent cognitive resilience and supporting precision psychiatry.

papers.title: Neural correlates underlying motor sequence task performance: handedness and sequence complexity.
papers.abstract: We aimed to determine the neural correlates of motor sequence performance in healthy young adults, with respect to handedness and sequence complexity. Strongly left-handed (LH, n = 15, 24.9y) and right-handed (RH, n = 15, 26.4y) participants performed finger key presses on a numeric keypad at four levels of sequence complexity with each hand in a randomized order. Both LH and RH performed the motor sequence task with faster reaction and motor execution times when using their right hand, irrespective of sequence complexity. Increasing motor-sequence complexity reduced frontal and parietal EEG power in both LH and RH, particularly at the highest complexity level, while RH also showed increased occipital delta activity when using the non-dominant hand, indicating that both sequence complexity and handedness modulate cortical activity during motor sequence performance. In addition, connectivity analysis showed significant hemispheric differences in brain network organization across frequency bands, with mainly greater left-hemisphere frontal and occipital connectivity but stronger right-hemisphere parietal connectivity. Sequence complexity primarily influenced functional connectivity (wPLI) rather than network topology. Notably, connectivity measures and selected MST-derived graph-theoretical metrics were linked to motor performance. Our findings suggest that motor-sequence performance is faster with the right hand, regardless of handedness and sequence complexity, which relies on a consistently organized hemispheric network, while increasing task complexity is managed primarily through frequency-specific changes in functional connectivity rather than large-scale reorganization of network structure.

papers.title: Developmental trajectories of pain empathy: evidence from drift diffusion modeling and EEG time-frequency analysis.
papers.abstract: Pain empathy develops from childhood into adulthood, but the cognitive and neural processes that support this development remain incompletely understood. The present study analyzed behavioral and electroencephalography (EEG) data from 120 participants (children, adolescents, and adults) who completed an Attention-to-Pain-Cue (A-P) task and an Attention-to-Non-Pain-Cue (A-N) task with painful and non-painful limb images. A hierarchical drift-diffusion model (HDDM) was used to characterize latent decision processes, and EEG time-frequency analyses were used to examine alpha- and beta-band event-related desynchronization (ERD). Across alternative DDM specifications, children showed lower drift rates, wider decision boundaries when averaged across image types, and longer non-decision times than older participants, which could be interpreted as differences in domain-general decision dynamics within pain-related task contexts. The EEG results showed age-related differences in alpha- and beta-band ERD, with reduced neural differentiation between painful and non-painful stimuli in children when pain cues were task-irrelevant. Together, these findings suggest that pain-related processing across development is shaped by both general maturation of decision processes and the increasing ability to maintain neural sensitivity to pain cues under changing attentional demands.

papers.title: Effects of environmental enrichments applied to pasture areas on free-range laying hens: 2. Pasture use, behaviour and welfare.
papers.abstract: 1. This study assessed the effects of environmental enrichment on outdoor ranges for birds aged either 25, 36, 48 and 56 weeks on pasture use, behaviour and welfare of free-range laying hens. In total, 900 hens (25 weeks old) were randomly divided into three groups (control, object enrichment and tree enrichment) with three pens each (100 hens/pen). Each group was provided with a closed shelter and pasture range nearby.2. A control (CON) group of birds was maintained without any extra enrichment. Various rectangular, square, cylindrical and triangle shaped boxes, pipes, buckets and structures in yellow, red and orange colour were used for the 'object' (OBJ) enrichment treatment, whereas tall and broad-leaved plants and Thuja trees were used for the 'tree' (TREE) enrichment treatment.3. The use of total pasture area in hens was not different amongst enrichment treatment groups or bird age. While the proportion of OBJ hens using the inner zone of the pasture was higher (p < 0.01), CON and TREE hen groups were found more in the outer zone of the pasture (p < 0.01).4. Enrichment treatment and age did not affect blood heterophil, lymphocyte and heterophil/lymphocyte (H/L) ratio. Feeding, drinking, walking, foraging, resting/laying, perching, scratching/preening and pecking behaviours were not different between enrichment treatment groups. Hens exhibited more feeding, drinking, walking, foraging and less perching, scratching/preening and pecking behaviours with age (p < 0.01).5. There were no differences in feather condition, comb wounds, foot pad dermatitis, keel bone damage, duration of tonic immobility or induction number amongst the enrichment groups. Older hens were showed significant deterioration in feather condition, increased occurrence of comb wounds, footpad dermatitis, hock burns and keel bone damage (p < 0.01). These findings indicated that environmental enrichment can increase the use of a specific area of the pasture where objects are used for enrichment.

papers.title: Psychometric Validation of the European Portuguese SWAL-QoL in Adults with Oropharyngeal Dysphagia After Neurological Injury: A Case-Control Study.
papers.abstract: Oropharyngeal dysphagia is common after neurological injury and substantially compromises health-related quality of life (HRQoL), yet no fully validated questionnaire is available for Portuguese-speaking adults with neurogenic dysphagia. In this cross-sectional case-control study, 255 adults were included: 85 with neurological injury and oropharyngeal dysphagia (case group), 70 with neurological injury without dysphagia, and 100 without neurological disease or swallowing complaints. All participants completed the European Portuguese SWAL-QoL; the neurological groups were additionally assessed with the Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS) and a standardized clinical swallowing evaluation. Internal consistency, test-retest reliability, exploratory factor analysis at item and domain level, convergent/divergent validity with FOIS, and clinical validity across groups and food and liquid consistencies were examined. The Portuguese SWAL-QoL showed excellent internal consistency (total Cronbach's α = 0.96; domains 0.72-0.97) and good to excellent test-retest reliability (r = .75-0.96). Inter-domain correlations ranged from 0.72 to 0.96. Item-level exploratory factor analysis explained 85.6% of the variance (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin, 0.93), and domain-level analysis revealed two higher-order factors - dysphagia-related and general HRQoL - explaining 69.2% of the variance (KMO, 0.90). Convergent validity with FOIS was moderate (r = .43), and clinical validity was supported by significantly lower scores in dysphagic participants for all domains except Sleep and by poorer scores with more restrictive diet consistencies. The European Portuguese SWAL-QoL is a reliable and valid instrument for assessing dysphagia-related HRQoL in adults with neurological injury and oropharyngeal dysphagia and is suitable for clinical practice and research in Portuguese-speaking settings. Oropharyngeal dysphagia; Health-related quality of life; SWAL-QoL; Psychometric validation; Neurological injury; Patient-reported outcome measures.

papers.title: Effects of environmental enrichments applied to pasture areas on free-range laying hens: 1. Performance and egg quality.
papers.abstract: 1. This study assessed the effects of environmental range enrichments, bird age and their interactions on laying performance and egg quality from Lohmann Brown hens.2. In total, 900 hens (25 weeks old) were randomly divided into three groups (control, object [OE] and tree [TE] enrichment) with three pen replicates each (100 hens/pen). Each pen was a closed shelter with pasture access nearby. Variously rectangular, square, cylindrical and triangle shaped, red, orange and yellow-coloured boxes, pipes, buckets and structures were used for the OE group, whereas tall and broad-leaved plants and Thuja trees were used for the tree enrichment group.3. Laying performance and egg quality traits were measured at 25-32, 33-40, 41-48 and 49-56 weeks of age.4. Significant differences in egg production were found amongst all groups (p < 0.01) due to differences in mortality at the start of the experimental period (p <<0.001). There were no significant differences between treatments in hen-day egg production. Environmental enrichment significantly decreased the albumen index and affected dirty egg ratio, shell thickness (p < 0.01) and shell weight (p < 0.05). Shell weight showed an interaction between enrichment and age (p < 0.01).5. Age had a significant effect on all performance and egg quality traits (p < 0.05), with 48-week-old hens generating the highest egg mass and hen-day and hen-housed egg production levels (p < 0.01).6. Although environmental enrichment can potentially increase egg production slightly, TE and OE resulted in fewer clean eggs. However, positive effects on albumen and shell quality traits were evident in the OE group.

papers.title: Smiling Muscle Stimulation Alters Neural Processing During Emotional Face Comparison.
papers.abstract: Within embodied and predictive-processing frameworks, emotional face perception is informed by bodily states, such as proprioceptive facial feedback. In line with this, our earlier work showed that activation of smiling muscles with facial neuromuscular electrical stimulation (fNMES) can induce a happiness bias in emotional face perception, and reduce visual face processing demands. Here, we extended this research to examine whether the same facial muscle stimulation biases the emotional representation of a face when it serves as a perceptual template (prime) for comparison with a following target face. In a delayed matching-to-sample task, 53 participants judged which of two sequentially presented faces appeared happier (or more female, in a control sex task). On half of trials, fNMES was applied bilaterally to the zygomaticus major during encoding of the prime face. Performance was held constant using an adaptive staircase. fNMES altered comparison judgments only when emotion was task-relevant, flattening the relation between emotion difference and choice. Across tasks, fNMES reduced N170 amplitudes and increased Early Posterior Negativity (EPN) differences between happy and sad faces. The prime EPN predicted choice only when emotion was task-relevant, whereas fNMES modulated emotion effects on the target N170 only in the control task. Facial feedback may thus increase the perceptual salience of emotion-relevant information, with task-dependent consequences for decisions.

papers.title: Trust Modulates Speech Entrainment: Enhanced Cortical Tracking for Low-trust Speakers.
papers.abstract: Trust is a critical component of human communication, providing a foundation for understanding, information exchange, and social coordination. Much of the research on trust in speech communication has focused on how vocal characteristics impact perceived trustworthiness. However, little is known about how trust in a speaker affects the neural processing of speech. Here, we demonstrate a two-stage experimental framework to study that question using noninvasive EEG. First, participants engage in a trust-building stage, where they play an investment game with fictional characters, each paired with a distinctive voice and trustworthiness level (i.e., frequency and magnitude of lies). Next, participants engage in a story-listening stage, in which they are presented with stories from the same characters. Data acquired from 20 young adults confirm a statistically significant correlation between the perceived and actual trustworthiness of the fictional characters. Cortical speech tracking was quantified using a temporal response function analysis on the EEG data. We found that the trustworthiness established during the trust-building stage influenced the cortical tracking of speech in the subsequent story-listening stage, with lower trustworthiness corresponding to a stronger cortical tracking of speech. Interestingly, trustworthiness selectively modulated tracking strength, with no statistically significant changes in the spatial and temporal temporal response function dynamics.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Spectral Power in Young Adults With Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Self-Reported Habitual Short Sleep: A Case-Control Study.
papers.abstract: Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) and insufficient sleep frequently co-occur during early adulthood, yet resting-state electroencephalographic (EEG) evidence in this population remains limited. The present study aimed to characterize resting-state EEG spectral power in young adults with GAD who also reported habitual short sleep, compared with healthy controls. This exploratory case-control study included 56 university students: 28 participants with GAD and self-reported habitual short sleep and 28 healthy controls. Resting-state EEG spectral power was quantified in the delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands. We retained unadjusted group comparisons for description and fitted age- and sex-adjusted linear models for the primary inferential interpretation. Channel-wise models likewise included group, age, and sex, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the 30 channels within each frequency band. After adjustment for age and sex, group coefficients remained positive for delta (2.51, 95% CI: 0.20 to 4.82), theta (2.52, 95% CI: 0.29 to 4.74), alpha (2.46, 95% CI: -0.12 to 5.03), and beta power (2.14, 95% CI: 0.13 to 4.15), but none met the FDR threshold (adjusted FDR p = 0.0501, 0.0501, 0.0608, and 0.0501, respectively). In unadjusted analyses, delta, theta, and beta differences survived FDR correction (FDR p = 0.0480 for each), whereas alpha did not (FDR p = 0.0553). In adjusted channel-wise analyses, 26 channel-by-band comparisons across 15 channels survived within-band FDR correction; all occurred in delta or theta and were concentrated over posterior and centroparietal electrodes. Whole-scalp estimates were directionally higher in the GAD plus habitual short-sleep group, but no age- and sex-adjusted frequency-band comparison survived FDR correction. Adjusted exploratory channel-wise findings indicated a posterior and centroparietal concentration in delta and theta power. These estimates remain preliminary and do not permit attribution to GAD, habitual short sleep, or their interaction.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Neurology: A Critical Narrative Review of Clinical Evidence, Translation, and Responsible Implementation.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to neuroimaging, electrophysiology, clinical text, and digitally measured behavior, but reported performance often exceeds the maturity of clinical evidence. We conducted a structured narrative review, informed by SANRA principles, of English-language human studies, reviews, and regulatory sources identified in PubMed/MEDLINE and IEEE Xplore from January 2022 through July 2026; older landmark studies were retained when necessary for historical or methodological context. We applied a common translational-evidence framework across six prespecified neurological domains to distinguish technical performance from external validation, prospective clinical evaluation, implementation, and demonstrated patient benefit. Evidence was appraised according to cohort representativeness, patient-level data separation, external and prospective validation, calibration, clinical comparators, regulatory status, workflow integration, and patient-level benefit. Across stroke, dementia, Parkinson disease, epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, and neuro-oncology, the strongest evidence concerns narrowly defined imaging and signal-processing tasks. A cluster-randomized stroke study demonstrated shorter thrombectomy workflow time, and several externally validated models show improved portability. In contrast, many high-accuracy classification and segmentation studies remain retrospective, single-dataset, internally validated, and uncalibrated. Multimodal learning, foundation models, federated learning, and large language models broaden capability but introduce additional risks related to dataset shift, bias, opacity, privacy, and automation. Neuro-AI should be judged by its intended clinical task and evidence maturity rather than headline accuracy. Multicenter external validation, prospective workflow evaluation, calibration, subgroup reporting, human-factors testing, and post-deployment surveillance are prerequisites for safe and equitable clinical use.

papers.title: Neurocognitive Processing of Visual Design in Digital Learning: Roles of Dynamic Color and Visual Texture in Learning Engagement.
papers.abstract: Dynamic color and visual texture are pervasive features of digital learning materials, yet their neurocognitive effects during learning remain insufficiently characterized. The authors investigated 26 university students using a 3 × 2 within-subject design comprising three dynamic color trajectories and two visual texture conditions (Smooth and Rough), while 64-channel EEG and condition-specific learning engagement were recorded. ERP and time-frequency analyses yielded temporally differentiated findings. Visual texture was associated with early P50 and theta activity, whereas an exploratory delta-band sensitivity analysis did not identify a reliable texture difference. Lightness was associated with N100 and early theta-to-low-beta activity, and saturation was associated with P300, beta/low-gamma activity, and inter-trial coherence. Learning engagement differed significantly across dynamic color trajectories, F(2, 50) = 18.74, p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.429, and texture conditions, F(1, 25) = 62.32, p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.714, with higher engagement under Smooth than Rough. Mean P300 amplitude was positively associated with engagement in a linear mixed-effects model, β = 0.43, 95% CI [0.28, 0.58], p < 0.001. These findings suggest distinct relationships among perceptual processing, subsequent task-related neural responses, and subjective engagement.

papers.title: Sleep Efficiency Irregularity Links PTSD with Early Cardiovascular Dysfunction in Young Adults.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, with sleep disturbances representing a potential mechanistic link. While prior research has focused on sleep duration and quality, the role of sleep regularity, particularly night-to-night variability in sleep patterns, remains unclear in PTSD as it relates to elevated CVD risk. Thus, this study examined whether sleep regularity is associated with key CVD precursors in young adults with PTSD. Methods: Twenty-eight individuals with a clinical diagnosis of PTSD and twenty-eight non-PTSD (CTRL) individuals (matched for age and sex) completed 7 days of wrist-worn actigraphy to assess sleep efficiency (SE) and total sleep time (TST), including their respective regularity (standard deviation). Oxidative stress (whole blood superoxide) and acute blood pressure control (cardiovagal baroreflex sensitivity (cBRS); Phase IV) were measured as indices of CVD risk. Results: Greater SE irregularity was significantly associated with higher oxidative stress and reduced cBRS in the PTSD group, indicating increased physiological stress and impaired acute blood pressure control. These relationships were not observed in CTRL. In contrast, TST regularity, as well as overall sleep duration and quality, were not associated with either CVD precursor in any group. Conclusion: These findings identify sleep efficiency regularity as an important correlate of early cardiovascular dysfunction in young adults with PTSD and extend previous observations linking sleep irregularity to cardiovascular risk in individuals experiencing chronic anxiety. Collectively, these findings highlight the potential importance of sleep regularity as a behavioral correlate of cardiovascular health across populations experiencing chronic psychological stress.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology

papers.title: Right heart remodeling in Sugen/hypoxia rat model of severe pulmonary hypertension.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) directly impacts the right heart through pressure overload. Unlike well-characterized remodeling of the left ventricle in systemic hypertension, PH-induced changes in the right heart are less understood. Here, we investigate chamber-specific alterations in the right atrium (RA) and right ventricle (RV) in a rat model of PH. PH was induced in 6-week-old male Wistar rats using Sugen/hypoxia (SuHx) treatment. Right heart pressure overload was confirmed by catheterization. Cardiac remodeling was characterized by using confocal microscopy, micro-CT, optical mapping, and proteomic mass spectrometry. The increase in right-heart mass was predominantly attributable to cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, with concomitant extracellular-matrix remodeling. Hypertrophy was associated with significantly elevated right heart pressures after SuHx treatment, further progressing during the subsequent normoxia. At the end of the PH protocol, electrophysiology analysis showed significant prolongation of the action potential in both the RA and RV. Proteomic analysis revealed pronounced alterations in the RV, with substantial overlap with the RA and LV, and more upregulated than downregulated proteins. GO analysis indicated increased expression of sarcomeric and fibrillar proteins and reduced expression of proteins related to oxidative energy production. In conclusion, myocardial remodeling in PH is based on cardiomyocyte hypertrophy rather than cell proliferation. Electrophysiological changes along with increased pressure in the right atrium might contribute to phenotype progression. Changes in proteome show commonalities and differences in RA and RV pressure-induced pathways that that warrant therapeutic exploration.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

papers.title: Direct patch-clamp recording reveals TRPML2-dependent cation conductance across pathogen-containing vacuole membranes.
papers.abstract: Transient receptor potential mucolipin 2 (TRPML2), a cation channel encoded by MCOLN2 and localized to endolysosomal compartments, has been implicated in restricting Salmonella enterica replication through regulation of the Salmonella-containing vacuole (SCV). However, direct electrophysiological evidence of TRPML2 activity on the SCV membrane has been lacking. Using S. enterica serovar Typhi as a model, we optimized infection and patch-clamp conditions to directly access SCVs in infected THP-1 cells and record vacuolar ion currents. SCVs from wild-type cells exhibited robust inward currents at negative potentials that were reduced in TRPML2-knockout cells and enhanced by TRPML2 agonists. Under Mg2+-permeant conditions, SCVs displayed TRPML2-dependent Mg2+ conductance, supporting a role for TRPML2 in regulating Mg2+ availability during S. Typhi infection. Ca2+-permeant recordings further showed agonist-responsive inward currents on SCVs, indicating that SCV-localized TRPML2 retains broader divalent-cation conductance. Basal currents were also better maintained on SCVs than on bacteria-negative vacuoles isolated from uninfected bystander cells within the same cultures. PI3P reduced current rundown, suggesting that the phosphoinositide environment of SCVs may help sustain TRPML2 activity. Together, these findings provide the first direct electrophysiological characterization of a pathogen-containing vacuole and establish a tractable platform for investigating host ion-channel function at the host-pathogen interface.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

papers.title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention.
papers.abstract: The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.

papers.title: Comorbidity of chronic musculoskeletal pain, depression, anxiety and sleep problems.
papers.abstract: Individuals with chronic pain (CP) are at elevated risk of mental health problems, but the awareness of this issue among patients as well as medical personnel is limited. Chronic musculoskeletal pain (CMP) is the most common type of CP. This narrative review summarizes the latest literature on the comorbidity of CMP with depression, anxiety and sleep problems. Around 40% of CP patients suffer from depression and/or anxiety of clinical severity. Sleep problems affect up to 75% of patients with CP. CMP. Depression, anxiety and impaired sleep are characterized by common underlying physiopathological mechanisms associated with serotonin and noradrenaline neurotransmission, glutamate/γ-aminobutyric acid signaling balance, low Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and altered immune system response. Comorbidity of depression, anxiety and sleep impairment is associated with decline in mental health, functioning and quality of life of the affected individuals, leading to a cumulative disability burden. Evidence supports cognitive behavioral therapy and acceptance and commitment therapy psychotherapies for CMP. Duloxetine is efficacious for pain relief, improvement of mood, anxiety, sleep and quality of life in CMP. Comorbidity of psychiatric issues among CMP patients is an unmet need which should be addressed to improve patient outcomes. Mental healthcare specialists ought to be integrated into the teams managing CMP patients.

papers.title: Circadian blood pressure dipping patterns, hypertension, and cortisol metabolism across the weight spectrum.
papers.abstract: Blood pressure (BP) exhibits a circadian rhythm with a nocturnal decline, dipping. Alterations in cortisol metabolism have been linked to hypertension and nondipping patterns. This study aimed to examine associations between 24-h BP patterns, hypertension, and cortisol levels. In this cross-sectional study, 426 participants (329 with BMI ≥30 kg/m2; 97 with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2) underwent 24-h ambulatory BP monitoring and assessments of 24-h urinary cortisol/cortisone ratio (F/E ratio), serum corticosteroid-binding globulin, and serum F/E ratio. Dippers were defined by at least 10% nocturnal BP fall; nondippers as less than 10% BP fall; and risers as a nocturnal BP increase. Participants with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2 (BMI 24.8 ± 2.7 kg/m2) compared to participants with BMI at least 30 kg/m2 (BMI 40.9 ± 6.8 kg/m2), were older (47.6 ± 8.2 vs. 43.9 ± 10.9, P = 0.002), had lower 24-h mean SBP (119 ± 11 vs. 131 ± 12 mmHg, P < 0.001), and were less frequently nondippers (50.5 vs. 66.6%, P = 0.004). No significant difference was observed in cortisol metabolism when comparing nondippers and dippers (sex-stratified). In a multivariable regression analysis, female sex, BMI at least 30 kg/m2, being normotensive, or receiving antihypertensive treatment were all significantly associated with a lower 24-h urinary F/E ratio. Among nondippers with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2, urinary F/E ratio was positively associated with 24-h mean SBP (r = 0.46, P < 0.001). Associations between cortisol biomarkers and BP variation were limited in participants with BMI at least 30 kg/m2, but appeared stronger in individuals with BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m2 with nondipping BP.

papers.title: Electrocardiographic markers of arrhythmic risk after renal sympathetic denervation in resistant hypertension.
papers.abstract: Renal sympathetic denervation (RDN) has emerged as a device-based therapy for resistant hypertension; however, its effects on electrocardiographic (ECG) markers related to arrhythmic risk remain incompletely defined. We aimed to evaluate changes in ECG indices reflecting atrial and ventricular electrical heterogeneity in patients undergoing RDN compared to medically treated controls. This retrospective cohort study included 263 patients with resistant hypertension (RDN+, n = 120; RDN-, n = 143) with baseline and 6-month ECG recordings. ECG parameters included the P-wave dispersion, Tp-Te interval, and frontal QRS-T angle. To account for baseline differences, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPW) based on propensity scores was applied. Weighted linear regression models with doubly robust adjustment were used to estimate the independent association between RDN and follow-up ECG parameters after adjusting for baseline ECG values and change in SBP. At 6 months, patients undergoing RDN demonstrated significantly lower P-wave dispersion (27.4 vs. 37.5 ms, P < 0.001), Tp-Te interval (80.3 vs. 84.7 ms, P = 0.028), and frontal QRS-T angle (26 vs. 37°, P = 0.026) compared with controls. In the weighted models, RDN remained independently associated with reductions in these parameters. In patients with resistant hypertension, renal sympathetic denervation was associated with improvements in ECG markers related to arrhythmic risk at 6 months, which were not fully explained by changes in office SBP.

papers.title: Multiparametric cardiomyocyte profiling with single-LED excitation reveals subtype-specific electromechanical coupling in LQTS in vitro.
papers.abstract: Cardiac excitation-contraction coupling (ECC) is an essential and tightly regulated process that links action potentials to intracellular calcium release and mechanical contraction. At the whole-heart level, ECC is captured by integrative evaluation of electrical and mechanical components of the cardiac cycle through parameters termed electromechanical delay (EMD) and electromechanical window (EMW). Alterations in the EMD or EMW reflect impaired electromechanical coupling and have been associated with increased arrhythmic risk across multiple cardiac diseases. However, it is currently unclear whether and how equivalent metrics can be derived and interpreted in vitro or meaningfully applied to patient-specific human disease models. Here, we implement ECC profiling in vitro using a single-LED optical imaging system that enables simultaneous measurements of membrane voltage, intracellular calcium and contractility. This approach allows quantification of individual transients and their temporal relationships. To investigate distinct perturbations of ECC, we applied this platform to human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) representing three mechanistically distinct ECC perturbations: a repolarization defect (LQT2, KCNH2 p.A561V), a calmodulin-associated calcium-handling defect (CALM-LQTS, CALM1 p.F142L) and pharmacological contractile uncoupling by myosin ATPase inhibition (blebbistatin). Cellular analogues of the clinical EMD and EMW were robustly quantifiable and provided mechanistically informative ECC signatures that were not entirely captured by conventional metrics focused on asynchronous individual transient analysis. Pharmacological targeting of the main cardiac ion currents further validated these findings and confirmed the robustness of the ECC quantification. This novel technique provides a basis for more sensitive assessment of disease phenotypes, arrhythmogenic risk and pharmacological effects in human cellular models, supporting the development of new approach methodologies. KEY POINTS: A single-LED optical platform enables fully synchronized, simultaneous measurement of voltage, calcium and contraction in human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes (CMs) at a high spatial and temporal resolution. In vitro analogues of the clinical electromechanical delay and electromechanical window can be robustly quantified in hiPSC-CM monolayers and behave consistently with their in vivo counterparts under genetic and pharmacological perturbations. Despite comparable APD80 prolongation, LQT2 and CALM-LQTS hiPSC-CMs display divergent electromechanical signatures, demonstrating that integrative ECC metrics resolve mechanistic differences not captured by conventional single-transient analyses. Pharmacological recapitulation of the disease phenotypes further confirmed these observations. In vitro ECC profiling offers a sensitive approach for distinguishing mechanistic perturbations of cardiac function and improving the characterization of arrhythmogenic risk.

papers.title: SL-S4Wave: Self-Supervised Learning of Physiological Waveforms with Structured State Space Models.
papers.abstract: Modeling long-sequence medical time series data, such as electrocardiograms (ECG), poses significant challenges due to high sampling rates, multichannel signal complexity, inherent noise, and limited labeled data. While recent self-supervised learning (SSL) methods, based on various encoder architectures such as convolutional neural networks, have been proposed to learn representations from unlabeled data, they often fall short in capturing long-range dependencies and noise-invariant features. Structured state space models (S4) excel at long-sequence modeling, but existing S4 architectures fail to capture the unique characteristics of multichannel physiological waveforms. In this work, we propose SL-S4Wave, a self-supervised learning framework that combines contrastive learning with a tailored encoder built on structured state space models. The encoder incorporates multi-layer global convolution using multiscale subkernels, enabling the capture of both fine-grained local patterns and long-range temporal dependencies in noisy, high-resolution multichannel waveforms. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that SL-S4Wave (1) consistently outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and self-supervised baselines in a challenging arrhythmia detection task, (2) achieves high performance with significantly fewer labeled examples, showcasing strong label efficiency, and (3) maintains robust performance on long waveform segments, highlighting its capacity to model complex temporal dynamics in long sequences that most existing approaches fail to efficiently model, and (4) transfers effectively to unseen arrhythmia types, underscoring its robust cross-domain generalization. We additionally evaluate SL-S4Wave on multiple EEG tasks, achieving superior performance over strong baselines, demonstrating generalizability of our approach beyond cardiac waveforms.

papers.title: The prevalence and risk factors associated with obesity among adults in Hawtat Bani Tamim: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Obesity has emerged as a significant public health issue in Saudi Arabia, showing regional variations in its prevalence and associated risk factors. This study provides the first city-level estimates of obesity prevalence and its independent sociodemographic and lifestyle determinants in Hawtat Bani Tamim, addressing the gap in localized epidemiological data for targeted public health interventions. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 384 adults living in Hawtat Bani Tamim. Sociodemographic, lifestyle, and clinical data were collected through standardized questionnaires and anthropometric measurements. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with obesity. The prevalence of obesity in the study population was 28.9%. Increased odds of obesity were observed in individuals aged 41-50 years (OR = 1.45, p = 0.001) and 51-60 years (OR = 2.40, p < 0.001), males (OR = 1.20, p = 0.007), those with lower education levels (secondary school or less, OR = 4.18, p = 0.008), short sleep duration (OR = 1.25, p = 0.021), smokers (OR = 1.30, p = 0.008), physically inactive individuals (OR = 1.60, p = 0.005), and those with hypertension. Moderate activity was protective (OR = 0.75, p = 0.028). There is no significant association between obesity and place of residence, marital status, occupation, or most dietary factors. Obesity is prevalent among adults in Hawtat Bani Tamim and is closely linked to age, gender, education level, sleep hours, smoking, physical inactivity, and hypertension. These results highlight the importance of targeted public health efforts and policies to reduce obesity rates and prevent related health issues in this area.

papers.title: Sleep bruxism in children is associated with multiple dimensions of anxiety.
papers.abstract: To evaluate overall and domain-specific anxiety in children with and without sleep bruxism using the multidimensional Spence Children's Anxiety Scale - Parent Version (SCAS-P). A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted in pediatric patients aged 7-12 years attending a university dental clinic. Sleep bruxism was assessed according to the ICSD-3 criteria. The Spence Children's Anxiety Scale - Parent Version (SCAS-P), considering both the total score and individual subscales, was applied to all subjects for a multidimensional assessment of anxiety. Group comparisons between children with sleep bruxism (SB) and without sleep bruxism (No-SB) were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test at p=0.05. Of the 122 children who met the inclusion criteria and were included in the analysis, 88 were classified as having SB. Children with SB showed significantly higher total anxiety scores compared with children without SB (p=0.002). Higher scores were also observed in children with SB for panic/agoraphobia, separation anxiety, physical injury fears, and social phobia (all p<0.05), with small-to-moderate effect sizes. Sleep bruxism in children is associated with higher anxiety levels, particularly in specific anxiety domains. These findings highlight the relevance of psychosocial assessment in pediatric patients.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental dentistry

papers.title: Neurologic presentation unmasks arrhythmogenic channelopathy: KCNH2 variant Long-QT syndrome managed with subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. A case report.
papers.abstract: A previously healthy 10-year-old boy developed febrile seizure-like episodes after an appendectomy, which were diagnosed as epilepsy despite a normal electroencephalogram. He later presented with dyspnea and palpitations and was prescribed propafenone for frequent premature ventricular complexes. The electrocardiogram showed a markedly prolonged QTc interval of 550 ms with a notched T wave in lead V2. Phenytoin and propafenone were discontinued, and propranolol was initiated, but QTc prolongation persisted. The combination of severely prolonged QTc, characteristic T-wave morphology, and absence of structural heart disease redirected the diagnosis toward a repolarization channelopathy; genetic testing confirmed long-QT syndrome type 2 due to a pathogenic KCNH2 c.1814C>T variant. β-blocker therapy was optimized, QT-prolonging triggers were avoided, and a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted. Cascade genetic screening identified no additional KCNH2 carriers. One variant-negative sister had frequent idiopathic right ventricular outflow tract premature ventricular complexes and was referred for catheter ablation.
papers.journal: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular

papers.title: Effect of Intraoperative Subanesthetic-Dose Esketamine on Postoperative Hydromorphone Consumption After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated whether intraoperative subanesthetic-dose esketamine reduces postoperative opioid consumption and improves early recovery outcomes after total hip arthroplasty (THA). A total of 128 patients was randomized to receive esketamine (Group E, n = 64) or saline (Group C, n = 64). Group E received an intravenous esketamine bolus of 0.25 mg/kg 5 minutes before skin incision, followed by a 0.25 mg/kg/h infusion until skin closure. Group C received an equivalent volume of normal saline using the same regimen. Postoperative analgesia was provided by patient-controlled intravenous analgesia with hydromorphone. The primary outcome was the cumulative hydromorphone consumption during the first 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included 48-h hydromorphone consumption, Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores, quality of recovery (QoR-15), Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS), mood, and adverse events. Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) was assessed as an exploratory outcome. The first 24-h hydromorphone consumption was significantly lower in Group E than in Group C (2.24 [2.08-2.51] vs 3.20 [2.88-3.40] mg, P < 0.001). Cumulative hydromorphone consumption over the first 48 h was also lower in Group E (4.40 [4.16-4.82] vs 5.92 [5.30-6.23] mg, P < 0.001). Group E had lower NRS scores at 6 and 24 h. On postoperative day 1, Group E exhibited higher QoR-15 scores and lower AIS scores (P < 0.05), and the incidence of PSD was significantly lower in Group E than in Group C (26.6% vs 54.7%, P = 0.001). Adverse event rates did not differ significantly between groups (P > 0.05). Intraoperative subanesthetic-dose esketamine reduced the first 24-h hydromorphone consumption after THA. Findings for the secondary outcomes are exploratory and require confirmation in future studies. ChiCTR2600116506.

papers.title: Visual Target P3b Amplitude Mediates the Relationship between Childhood Traumatic Experiences and Social Functioning in People at Clinical High Risk for Psychosis.
papers.abstract: Clinical high risk (CHR) for psychosis status is associated with poor social functioning. Previous studies suggest that childhood trauma and reduced amplitude of the P300 event-related potential (ERP) component elicited by infrequent target stimuli (P3b) are associated with poor social function. Here, we examined whether reduced P3b mediates the relationship between reported trauma history and social function in CHR individuals, possibly reflecting the impact of past trauma on neurophysiological processes subserving attention that ultimately influence social functioning. Target P3b ERP amplitudes from visual and auditory oddball tasks acquired at baseline in the Accelerating Medicines Partnership Schizophrenia (AMP SCZ) study were analyzed. The mediating effects of auditory and visual P3b amplitude on the relationship between trauma history (Childhood Trauma Questionnaire total score) and Negative Symptom Inventory-Psychosis Risk Asociality (NSI-PR) as well as social functioning (Global Functioning: Social (GFS) scores were examined. Data from 931 CHR participants (average age 21.29 years, 36.3% male) were included in mediation analyses. Visual P3b showed significant (P < .05) mediation of the relationship between trauma load and GFS score (5.4% mediation) as well as mediation of the relationship between trauma history and NSI-PR asociality (9.3% mediation). Auditory P3b did not significantly mediate either relationship. These results suggest that visual, but not auditory, P3b mediates the relationship between past trauma load and social functioning in CHR, suggesting the effect of trauma on the neurophysiological processes subserving visual target detection may contribute to social functioning deficits in CHR individuals.
