papers.title: Regulatory role of TIPE2 by inhibiting microglial pyroptosis and glycolysis in the treatment of sepsis-associated encephalopathy.
papers.abstract: Sepsis_associated encephalopathy (SAE) denotes acute cerebral dysfunction triggered by sepsis and is accompanied by high mortality. Our previous study showed that TIPE2 significantly ameliorated cognitive impairment in SAE mice by inhibiting neuroinflammation, but the specific mechanism was unknown. TIPE2 expression and cell specificity were analysed by scRNA‑seq and immunofluorescence. To establish SAE, cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) was carried out in TIPE2 knockout (KO) and WT mice. Neuronal/synaptic damage was assessed by TUNEL and TEM; cognitive function by behavioural tests and EEG. Hippocampal scRNA‑seq compared WT and TIPE2 KO mice. In vitro, primary microglia and BV2 cells were stimulated with LPS/nigericin. Protein expression (Western blot/IF), RhoA activation (GST‑pulldown), glucose/lactate levels, ROS production, and TIPE2‑RhoA interaction (Co‑IP/confocal) were examined. scRNA‑seq confirmed that TIPE2 is predominantly expressed in microglia and downregulated in SAE; its deficiency promotes pro‑inflammatory microglia associated with pyroptosis and glycolysis. TIPE2 KO significantly aggravated cognitive impairment, promoted M1 polarisation, enhanced pyroptosis (GSDMD cleavage, caspase‑1 activation), and increased ROS production. Mechanistically, TIPE2 directly bound to RhoA and inhibited its activation, thereby suppressing NLRP3‑mediated pyroptosis and glycolysis in microglia. Treatment with the RhoA‑specific inhibitor Rhosin reversed TIPE2 deficiency‑induced microglial polarisation, pyroptosis, ROS production, and glycolytic reprogramming, and also ameliorated cognitive dysfunction in TIPE2 KO mice. TIPE2 protects against SAE by directly interacting with RhoA, inhibiting its activation, and subsequently suppressing NLRP3‑mediated microglial pyroptosis and glycolysis.

papers.title: Socioeconomic status and long-term risk of inflammatory bowel disease: a prospective cohort study with mediation analysis.
papers.abstract: The association of socioeconomic status with incident inflammatory bowel disease and the contribution of lifestyle factors remain unclear. We aimed to comprehensively investigate the association between socioeconomic status (SES) and the risk of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and to assess the mediating effect of lifestyle factors in a prospective cohort. We assessed SES using household income, education level, and employment status, and categorised participants into high-, medium-, and low-SES groups using latent profile analysis. We combined lifestyle factors, including smoking, alcohol consumption, diet, physical activity, body mass index, and sleep duration, to calculate a healthy lifestyle score as a mediator. The primary outcome was incident IBD. We used Cox proportional hazards models and mediation analysis to examine associations between SES and incident IBD and to assess the mediation effect. Participants free of IBD at baseline were included (n = 374,507), with a mean age of 55.84 years, of whom 51.5% were female. Overall, 76,292 (20.4%) were classified as high, 197,130 (52.6%) as medium, and 101,085 (27.0%) as low patterns. Over 14.57 years of follow-up, we identified 2381 incident IBD cases, 1703 ulcerative colitis (UC) and 843 Crohn's disease (CD), with an overall incidence rate of 44.9 per 100,000 person-years. After multivariable adjustment, a high SES pattern was associated with a 45% lower IBD risk compared to low SES (hazard ratio (HR) = 0.55; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.48-0.63). Meanwhile, all SES components showed beneficial effects, with higher education level demonstrating the strongest association (HR = 0.58; 95% CI = 0.51-0.65). The combination of high SES and healthy lifestyle conferred the greatest protection (HR = 0.37; 95% CI = 0.29-0.46). Mediation analyses indicated that lifestyle factors explained 11.34-16.50% of the observed association between SES and incident IBD. Similar protective associations were observed for both UC and CD. Healthy lifestyle factors partially explained the association between SES and incident IBD. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational design, potential residual confounding, and assumption-dependent mediation estimates.

papers.title: Sleep-like slow waves in wakefulness index post-stroke behavioural alterations.
papers.abstract: Increases in high-amplitude, low-frequency EEG oscillations during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep serve as markers of neuronal silencing, which disrupts functional connectivity and is associated with a loss of awareness and responsiveness. Cortical slowing likewise occurs during wakefulness, upon sleep deprivation, and accompanies performance deterioration. Recent work has revealed similar oscillations (termed 'sleep-like slow waves') following stroke in brain regions close or connected to a brain lesion, offering a plausible but untested mechanism for stroke-related behavioural impairment. Here, we simultaneously recorded EEG and behavioural performance while 30 unilateral stroke patients (12 left hemisphere, 18 right hemisphere) and 27 age-matched healthy adults completed a computerised perceptual decision-making task. Stroke patients had predominantly middle cerebral artery strokes (n=25), with a small subset of posterior cerebral artery (n=4), and anterior cerebral artery/middle cerebral artery (n=1) lesions. Sleep-like slow waves occurred more frequently in stroke patients relative to healthy controls, with limited spatial specificity when comparing patients with left and right lesion sites (more slow waves ipsilateral of the lesion). Furthermore, there was a significant correlation between slow wave occurrence and the accuracy and speed of perceptual reports in stroke patients, suggesting that variations in the occurrence of slow waves may contribute to cognitive heterogeneity post-stroke. As sleep-like slow waves predict deficits in perceptual decision-making following stroke, they represent a plausible mechanism of post-lesion functional network dysfunction extending beyond the damaged regions, thereby contributing to broader cognitive impairments.

papers.title: Enlightening pregnancy as a potential pathway to protect maternal circadian functioning and postpartum mood.
papers.abstract: The perinatal period is characterized by profound psychological, physiological, and behavioral changes that may increase sleep, circadian, and affective disturbances. While sleep disruption across pregnancy and postpartum has been widely documented, far less is known about how this transition shapes circadian health and whether circadian characteristics during pregnancy predict postpartum circadian and affective outcomes. In this study, we characterize circadian preference, circadian phase, circadian function, and light exposure across the transition from late pregnancy to early postpartum, and examine their predictive value for postpartum circadian function and depressive and anxiety symptomatology. Women were followed from the third trimester of pregnancy to 1 month postpartum. At both time points, participants wore a wrist actigraph to derive circadian parameters including the circadian function index (CFI) and circadian phase (L5c), and to quantify mean light exposure. Circadian preference and affective states were also assessed by questionnaires (MEQ, EPDS, STAI-T). Within-subject changes from pregnancy to postpartum were examined, and regression models were used to test whether prenatal circadian and affective measures predicted postpartum circadian function and depressive symptomatology. The transition to postpartum was marked by a significant reduction in CFI and mean light exposure, whereas circadian preference and L5c remained largely stable. During pregnancy, higher CFI was associated with morningness and greater light exposure; however, these associations were no longer evident postpartum. Postpartum CFI was predicted by prenatal CFI and circadian preference, with lower values observed among women with more evening-oriented profiles. In parallel, prenatal affective symptoms showed continuity into the postpartum period, and both prenatal CFI and circadian preference contributed to the prediction of postpartum depressive symptoms. Together, these findings indicate that early postpartum is characterized by a decay in circadian function rather than a shift in circadian phase, identify eveningness as a vulnerability factor during the transition to motherhood, support the use of CFI as an integrative marker of maternal circadian health, and highlight pregnancy as a potential window for circadian-informed interventions aimed at improving postpartum circadian and mood outcomes.

papers.title: Structural and EEG Motor Networks Distinguish Level of Motor Impairment After Stroke.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to determine how structural and EEG-based functional connectivity jointly distinguish levels of motor impairment after stroke. We estimated patient-specific (1) structural connectivity using MRI-derived lesion models and (2) functional connectivity using source-localized EEG, guided by each patient's structural connectome. Analyses focused on the brainstem and three motor-related cortical regions bilaterally: primary motor cortex (M1), dorsal premotor cortex (PMd), and supplementary motor cortex (SMA). Network analysis metrics (degree centrality, average efficiency, betweenness centrality) were applied to structural and functional data, contrasting motor networks between patients with high (H) and low (L) upper extremity motor function. Structural disconnection of the brainstem from M1 and PMd carried the highest probability of low motor status. All network measures were elevated in the H group compared to the L group across motor-related regions, indicating a globally strengthened motor network organization associated with better motor function. Functional connectivity revealed convergent but distinct patterns. In the delta band (1-3 Hz), ipsilesional motor regions showed stronger connectivity in the H group. In the beta band (14-29 Hz), contralesional motor regions demonstrated enhanced connectivity in H patients, consistent with prior evidence that contralesional motor regions may contribute to motor function after ipsilesional injury. We also introduced a novel metric, motor betweenness centrality, to quantify the role of nonmotor regions in rerouting motor-related communication. Almost all new hubs identified structurally were associated with lower motor status, suggesting less efficient network organization in more impaired patients. Thus, preservation of direct motor pathways supports better motor status, while reliance on alternative, less efficient routes correlates with worse outcomes. By contrast, EEG routing revealed that H patients recruited proximal cortical hubs, while L patients relied on distant, inefficient ones, highlighting functional network organization not evident in the structural analysis. These patterns suggest that more local network organization, rather than more distributed rerouting, is associated with better motor status within the motor system. In summary, multimodal network properties reliably identified key motor ROIs predictive of motor status. This concordance suggests that EEG-based metrics, particularly delta- and beta-band connectivity, are associated with lesion-derived structural disruption and complementary features of motor-network organization. Structural connectivity damage within motor circuits defines the extent of network disruption associated with motor impairment, while EEG functional connectivity provides complementary information about network organization measured at the time of assessment. Together, these measures characterize different aspects of motor network integrity after stroke.

papers.title: Melatonin in pediatric populations: promise or peril?
papers.abstract: This review summarizes both the current evidence from clinical trials examining the use of exogenous melatonin for insomnia in children and adolescents and the recent literature raising potential concerns regarding melatonin as an over-the-counter (OTC) supplement. Given a number of caveats and the existence of remaining knowledge gaps, the overall aim of the review is to assist healthcare practitioners in decision-making for their pediatric patients and families. While the evidence base supporting the efficacy and tolerability of melatonin for insomnia for children with neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism is generally considered robust, the literature in typically developing children is comparatively small. Studies over the past decade have raised concerns regarding the exponential increase in melatonin use in pediatric populations, reliability of the content of OTC melatonin products, the increase in accidental ingestions, especially in young children, and potential misuse of melatonin for unsupported indications. While melatonin has a role in the management of pediatric insomnia as well as of circadian rhythm disorders, the existing literature supports behavioral interventions as the first-line treatment option. Potential pitfalls in the clinical use of melatonin in children are important to recognize and incorporate into best-practice recommendations.

papers.title: Determination of changes in the nutrition and physical activity status of academicians during the pandemic period.
papers.abstract: To assess the changes in nutrition habits, physical activity levels, sedentary behaviours, sleep patterns and quality of academicians before and during the coronavirus disease-2019 pandemic. The descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted from January to September 2022 after approval from Karadeniz Technical University, Turkiye, and comprised academicians working at public universities in Turkiye during the coronavirus disease-2019 pandemic period. The survey questionnaire was distributed online to all public universities across the country. The participants' food consumption before and during the epidemic, sleep patterns and physical activity conditions were assessed. Data was analysed using SPSS 22. Of the 299 academicians,166(55.5%) were female and 133(45.5%) were male. Overall age range was 19-65 years, with 122(40.8%) subjects aged 35-44 years. A significant number of academicians 143(47.83%) reported changes in their eating habits, while even more 189(64.29%) indicated that a sedentary lifestyle had a negative impact on their health. There was a significant increase in the number of snacks (p<0.001). A total of 125(42.09%) participants reported using nutritional supplements during the pandemic, with vitamins, multivitamins and minerals being the most commonly chosen options. A significant majority of participants 178(59.73%) reported changes in sleep patterns and weight-gain during the pandemic. The time spent watching TV and using computers, tablets and phones increased significantly during the isolation period (p<0.05). Also, there was a decrease in the physical activities of the academicians (p<0.05). Even within more aware segments of the population, such as academicians, the coronavirus disease- 2019 pandemic's impact on psychological wellbeing led to significant alterations in eating, sleeping and physical activity patterns.

papers.title: Ambipolar Fiber Amplifiers for Highly Sensitive Biosignal Detection.
papers.abstract: Biological signals are inherently weak and susceptible to noise, making in situ signal amplification critical for high-fidelity sensing. Electronic fibers offer unique advantages for conformal and scalable biointegration; however, fiber amplifiers are seldom reported due to the lack of suitable semiconducting materials that combine balanced ambipolar transport, scalable fiber fabrication, and high device performance. Herein, we report the first single-component ambipolar fiber platform based on a newly designed polymer, P(gTDPP-TQ), which combines balanced p- and n-type transport, low-cost synthesis, and continuous fiber fabrication. Fiber processing enhances molecular ordering and charge transport, yielding record-high µC* and gm,norm among reported semiconducting fibers, enabling high-performance fiber amplifiers with a high voltage gain of up to 150 V V-1 and low operating voltages down to 0.5 V. These fiber amplifiers enable high-fidelity electroencephalogram signal amplification over 20 times and sensitive cortisol sensing with a record-low detection limit of 3.7 fM. This work establishes a general ambipolar fiber platform for integrated bioelectronic amplification and sensing.

papers.title: Burnout and Related Occupational and Psychological Outcomes Among Emergency Nurses in Saudi Arabia: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: To map primary Saudi studies reporting burnout, occupational fatigue, anxiety, depression, psychological distress, or sleep disturbance among emergency-department (ED) nurses. Scoping review. Following PRISMA-ScR, PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL Complete, ProQuest Nursing & Allied Health and Web of Science Core Collection were searched on 15 September 2026 using PCC-based controlled vocabulary and free-text terms. Primary quantitative, qualitative and mixed-methods studies (1 January 2015-15 September 2026) that meet the inclusion criteria were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardized form, resolving disagreements by discussion. Charted data covered design, setting, sample and ED-nurse denominator, outcome construct and instrument, scoring, nurse-specific results and associations. Synthesis was descriptive and grouped by construct; meta-analysis was not planned given heterogeneity in constructs, measures, thresholds and reporting. The four sources yielded 1694 raw record instances; 15 Saudi ED-nurse records were included. Seven quantitative reports measured burnout, while two qualitative studies described burnout-related experiences. Other records examined fatigue, anxiety/depression, occupational stress, or secondary traumatic stress. Variation in measures, thresholds, sampling and reporting precluded meta-analysis or a defensible pooled estimate. Evidence from selected Saudi emergency settings signals concerns across burnout and related outcomes, but limited geographic coverage and predominantly cross-sectional designs preclude national prevalence or causal conclusions. Distinguishing burnout from adjacent constructs is essential. Nursing leaders should monitor constructs separately using validated tools and ED-nurse-specific denominators, and pair confidential support with organizational action on modifiable work conditions. Future multisite longitudinal and intervention studies should assess feasibility and outcomes before wider adoption.

papers.title: SERPINE1 Identifies a Shared Injury-associated Molecular Signature in Intracerebral Hemorrhage and Epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and epilepsy are clinically linked neurological disorders, yet their shared molecular features remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify shared molecular candidates across ICH and epilepsy by integrating transcriptomic data with a curated set of genes with established circadian relevance. Transcriptomic datasets for ICH and epilepsy were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus, and candidate genes were curated from the Molecular Signatures Database and GeneCards. Differentially expressed candidate genes were intersected, and an integrative machine-learning framework-including Boruta, LASSO, XGBoost, and CatBoost-was applied to prioritize shared genes. Integrated machine-learning and network analyses nominated SERPINE1 for further investigation. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis identified higher scores for porphyrin, folate and pterine, and arachidonic acid metabolism in both disease comparisons. SERPINE1 expression correlated positively with arachidonic acid metabolism scores in both datasets, while Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis linked its expression to inflammatory transcriptional signatures, including TNFA signaling via NFKB and IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling. Gene interaction, drug-mRNA, transcription factor-mRNA, and competing endogenous RNA networks further characterized its regulatory and pharmacological context. Independent bulk transcriptomic datasets and experimental models supported SERPINE1 upregulation, with single-nucleus RNA-sequencing providing complementary cellular context, while single-nucleus analyses and immunostaining further supported its preferential microglial localization. Collectively, these findings identify SERPINE1 as a shared injury-associated molecular feature of ICH and epilepsy, with preferential microglial localization and associations with inflammatory transcriptional signatures and metabolic pathway scores. Although SERPINE1 is known to be clock-regulated, whether its temporal expression pattern is altered in ICH or epilepsy remains to be determined.

papers.title: In Situ Probing of Small-Molecule Electrolysis Using Ambient-Pressure X-Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic small-molecule conversion addresses the need to couple renewable electricity with sustainable fuel and chemical production, yet challenges remain in resolving the dynamic gas/solid/liquid interfaces that govern catalytic activity, selectivity and stability. A key challenge is to correlate catalyst structures, reaction intermediates and local interfacial environments under comparable operating conditions. Ambient-pressure x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provides surface-sensitive and chemically specific information on catalyst chemical states, interfacial species and local electrostatic environments at the same working interface, enabling direct correlations between catalyst evolution and reaction intermediates. We offer a forward-looking review of APXPS for probing gas/solid/liquid interfaces in small-molecule electrolysis. We discuss three categories of electrochemical XPS/APXPS configurations: quasi-in situ XPS, in which electrochemically treated catalysts are transferred under protected conditions for post-reaction analysis; thin-electrolyte-film (dip-and-pull) APXPS, which probes a potential-controlled interface through a nanometer-scale liquid film; and membrane-based APXPS, which accesses catalyst-ionomer-electrolyte interfaces. We introduce present-day challenges in electrochemical APXPS and describe a vision towards more realistic operating conditions, higher time resolution and multimodal measurements integrated with theoretical and data-driven spectral analysis. These developments provide potential avenues to establish reliable structure-intermediate-environment relationships in the further development of small-molecule electrocatalysis.

papers.title: A Preliminary Examination of Modulation of the LPP by Personal Preference Rankings for Pleasant Experiences.
papers.abstract: The late positive potential (LPP) is a robust neural marker of attention toward emotionally salient stimuli, yet it is unknown how the LPP is modulated by personal preferences for specific types of pleasant objects/experiences. The present study aimed to evaluate whether personal preferences for pleasant experiences modulate the LPP to images reflecting those situations. Secondary analyses examined whether depressive symptoms and a positive emotion intervention were associated with individual differences in this modulation. College students (N = 92; Mage = 19.44, SD = 1.15) reported depressive symptoms before randomization to a positive emotion intervention (n = 47) or study skills comparison group (n = 45). Participants then rank-ordered a list of eight categories of positive objects/experiences (e.g., cute animals, adventure, social activities, junk food) based on which they enjoyed most and viewed images of each while EEG data were recorded. The LPP was modulated by personal preferences broadly, such that the LPP to images depicting top-ranked pleasant categories was enhanced compared to low-ranked pleasant categories; however, significant effects were not observed linearly between each individual ranking. In secondary analyses, depressive symptoms moderated preference effects on the LPP, with greater symptoms associated with less differentiation between highly preferred and less preferred positive stimuli. The positive emotion intervention did not significantly impact LPP modulation by personal preference. Results highlight the utility of considering personal salience in selecting stimuli for clinical neuroscience tasks and indicate that depression may be characterized by difficulty sustaining attention to personally salient pleasant experiences.

papers.title: Sleep as a Modifiable Risk Factor for Progression to Substance Use Disorder: A Review of Applicability in Adolescents with Early Life Adversity.
papers.abstract: Substance use disorder (SUD) often originates in childhood and adolescence, with early life adversity (ELA) being a particularly potent risk factor increasing susceptibility. This narrative review explores the intricate relationships between ELA, sleep disturbances, and substance use in adolescents. We identified relevant articles through a PubMed search of keywords (ELA, sleep, substance use, adolescents), focusing on peer-reviewed research and reviews from the past three years, supplemented by reference list reviews and prior exposure based on previous work in the area. We examine psychological and neurobiological processes underlying ELA-induced sleep disturbances and substance use, as well as the bidirectional relationship between sleep and substance use. We also discuss the efficacy of sleep-focused interventions in improving mental health and reducing substance use, noting untested potential in ELA-exposed youth. By focusing on core but less studied pathways underlying substance use behaviors, such as internalizing psychopathology and subcortical circuits, future research can pave the way for innovative new interventions to significantly impact life trajectories in this vulnerable population.
